title: Australian politicians say they are paying thousands for their own security upgrades amid rising threats
summary: Security agencies will review safety precautions for MPs’ homes and offices after numerous federal politicians told police and Asio in safety briefings that they were worried about widening threats after the alleged attack on Helen Haines. The Labor government and politicians across the parliament a...
content:
Security agencies will review safety precautions for MPs’ homes and offices after numerous federal politicians told police and Asio in safety briefings that they were worried about widening threats after the alleged attack on Helen Haines.
The Labor government and politicians across the parliament are still considering how they will respond when they return to Canberra next week, with ideas being floated including a new committee on MPs’ safety, greater resources for police, and motions of condolence for Haines, who lost both her legs after Monday’s incident. Renewed calls from the crossbench for reforms to question time and the tone of debate in parliament are unlikely to be taken up by the major parties.
In safety briefings with the Australian federal police and Asio granted to Labor, Coalition and crossbench MPs on Wednesday, security of homes and electorate offices was a common concern, according to Guardian Australia interviews with 10 MPs. While a broad review of safety and security is unlikely at this stage, multiple MPs across the political spectrum told Guardian Australia they had spent thousands of dollars of their own money to install safety features based on the advice of the federal police.
Federal ministers receive stronger security assistance, but numerous backbenchers said they felt under-resourced, saying many angry constituents may see all politicians as a homogenous group, and may not differentiate between cabinet members and ordinary local MPs.
“People are getting activated now because they see us as part of the government. We represent the system to them, as much as anyone else,” independent Monique Ryan said.
Two years ago, the AFP recorded 951 reports of harassing and threatening behaviour against office holders. Last year, that increased to 1,067. On Wednesday, police arrested a man after he allegedly caused a disturbance at a Perth electorate office and was reported to have made verbal threats “while in possession of what has been described as nunchucks”. No one was injured as a result, Western Australia police said.
‘Not well protected’
A number of politicians asked to speak anonymously to discuss reflections from the briefings. While many praised the AFP’s response when their staff contacted them – for instance, to seek advice on holding public events – some said they had received less timely assistance from local police when they requested help, such as to respond to aggressive visitors.
Numerous MPs said they did not want security guards or armed escorts for themselves in public, but that they felt alarmed for the safety of their homes and families.
Some said they would feel more comfortable with cameras and floodlights at home, and had decided to pay for their own upgrades after not being offered such features in risk assessments conducted by security agencies. One independent MP said crossbenchers questioned whether extra home security features should be paid for by the public.
Several MPs said they wanted more security and safety support, but questioned how much impact that would have on their overall safety and how much more the AFP could do.
Guardian Australia was told security officials had committed to assessing safety settings of MPs who raised specific concerns. While a broad-ranging government review is at this stage not expected, other responses could include giving MPs more information on the background work that policing agencies conduct year-round, such as threat assessments and periodic checks.
The prime minister, Anthony Albanese, told News24 his government had overseen “an increase in funding for security for members of parliament in the last couple of years”.
“We want to make sure that people can feel as much comfort as possible, that everything’s being done to maximise security. But also, I think parliamentarians across the board are determined to make sure we can continue to engage as we need to in this great democracy of ours,” he said.
A spokesperson for the home affairs minister, Tony Burke, said: “Reviews of the threats faced by high office holders are constantly conducted by our agencies.”
Ryan, who is close with Haines, said she had rarely discussed safety arrangements with fellow MPs until recent times, but claimed many colleagues were “now realising they’re having common experiences”. She was supportive of a broader review into safety, and more resources to secure offices.
“If it makes my team feel better and safer to have bollards out the front, I’m happy,” she said.
Two Labor MPs said some government backbenchers had expressed frustrations towards the finance department for not adequately funding safety measures for their electorate offices or doing so in a timely way. One said money was “always an issue” with the department, and expected more MPs to be directly lobbying the prime minister to improve office security.
Nationals MP Sam Birrell, whose electorate neighbours Haines’s in Indi, said regional politicians had particular concerns, with many being highly visible in their communities and locals often knowing where they lived.
“Some of the MPs were frustrated there’s not clear advice on things like whether to advertise mobile offices or have signs on cars,” he said.
“There were some complaints about whether people are able to get fairly modest security measures … that needs to be reviewed.”
Multiple people across meetings raised concerns about how to protect electorate office staff.
Liberal senator James Paterson told Radio National electorate offices were “very exposed” and were “not well protected”.
Asio and AFP have been contacted for comment.

title: Majority of Australians who report penicillin allergy not truly allergic
summary: The majority of Australians who report a penicillin allergy are not truly allergic, prompting the peak body for immunologists to change its guidelines in a bid to reduce hospitals stays and tackle antimicrobial resistance. Penicillin, one of the most commonly prescribed antibiotics in Australia, was...
content:
The majority of Australians who report a penicillin allergy are not truly allergic, prompting the peak body for immunologists to change its guidelines in a bid to reduce hospitals stays and tackle antimicrobial resistance.
Penicillin, one of the most commonly prescribed antibiotics in Australia, was thought to cause allergies in 10% of Australians, or about 2.8 million people.
But the latest evidence shows up to 90% of those reporting a penicillin allergy do not have one.
The changes to the Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy guidelines, which have been published in the Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology, give the first peer-reviewed and updated advice to GPs and other health professionals about how to diagnose and manage the allergy, and when to refer to a specialist.
Prof Michaela Lucas, a clinical immunologist, said misdiagnosis occurs for a number of reasons, with people sometimes experiencing a rash or nausea after taking penicillin and assuming it’s an allergy, or doctors wanting to be cautious and recording side-effects as allergies.
Other people were told by a parent that they suffered a reaction when they were a child and carry that diagnosis through to adulthood without questioning it, she said, while some side-effects may also be due to the illness itself and not the medicine.
Penicillin is an important antibiotic option, as it treats common infections, said Lucas, a professor at the University of Western Australia’s medical school.
“It is also what is known as a narrow spectrum antibiotic, which means it is targeted at the bug specifically causing the infection,” she said.
“Once you have to avoid narrow classes of drugs, you have to use broader spectrum antibiotics which have a bigger impact of your gut microbiome as they are associated with also killing good bacteria and allowing superbugs to come in and take residency.”
Superbugs are strains of bacteria that are highly resistant to multiple standard treatments.
“Antimicrobial resistance matters beyond the individual patient, because resistant bacteria can spread between people and through communities,” Lucas said.
“If someone develops a serious infection that is resistant to several antibiotics, doctors can be left with very limited treatment options.”
Dr Nick Cooling, the chair of the Royal Australian College of General Practitioners’ allergy special interest group, said the guidelines were based on the latest evidence, and a consensus report from a range of medical specialities.
He hopes the guidance will cut health costs in the community and ease the burden on immunologists.
“We know that people who have a penicillin allergy label go to hospital more,” he said.
“They spend longer in hospital, and they also cost the system more.”
This is because of more treatments needing to be trialled, side-effects from those treatments, and delays in finding alternative treatments.
“The ability to clarify that with these patients will reduce hospital costs but also the whole health system cost,” he said.
“We need all health professionals to be involved in this because if we’re going to de-label some 2.8 million people in Australia, you can’t just rely on the 300 immunologists to do that.”
Cooling urged affected patients to raise the question of a penicillin allergy with their GP, and with cases where the potential risk of harm is low, doctors could give their patient penicillin and monitor for symptoms.
But he warned: “No one should try taking penicillin themselves to find out whether they are allergic. Antibiotics should only be taken when prescribed for the individual taking them.”
For Tammy Prescino, the issue of penicillin allergy is a very real concern. She welcomes the changes, with her 70-year-old mother and 12-year-old daughter both diagnosed.
Prescino worries that if her mother were to get an infection, she could miss out on the benefits of penicillin. She plans to see a doctor and to get her family reassessed.
“Because if she doesn’t have the penicillin allergy, then we wouldn’t have to withhold medicine … that could help her,” Prescino said.

title: Is Rabies Making a Comeback?

title: Principal Asset Management analiza el futuro de la inversión institucional en Insurance Forum 2026
summary: La inversión institucional atraviesa un periodo de transformación marcado por nuevas exigencias regulatorias, cambios en los mercados financieros y una creciente necesidad de diversificar los portafolios. Ante este escenario, Principal Asset Management reunió a especialistas internacionales, autorid...
content:
La inversión institucional atraviesa un periodo de transformación marcado por nuevas exigencias regulatorias, cambios en los mercados financieros y una creciente necesidad de diversificar los portafolios. Ante este escenario, Principal Asset Management reunió a especialistas internacionales, autoridades y representantes del sector asegurador durante el Insurance Forum 2026, celebrado el 13 de octubre en la Ciudad de México.
El encuentro, encabezado por Jesús Martín del Burgo, Head of Institutional Business Latam de Principal Asset Management, permitió analizar las tendencias que están redefiniendo las estrategias de inversión de las aseguradoras, así como las oportunidades para fortalecer la administración de activos y responder a compromisos financieros de largo plazo.
Uno de los principales temas fue la evolución del marco regulatorio y sus implicaciones para las decisiones de inversión. Jorge Otilio Avendaño Estrada, vicepresidente de Operación Institucional de la Comisión Nacional de Seguros y Fianzas, abordó los desafíos relacionados con la solvencia, la gestión de riesgos y las condiciones que enfrenta la industria para mantener portafolios sólidos en un entorno financiero cambiante.
La discusión también puso atención en la diversificación y el papel de los mercados privados dentro de las estrategias institucionales. Jack Bishop, Senior Managing Director, Strategic Initiatives - Private Markets de Principal, y Román Toledo, Managing Partner de Cedice, compartieron perspectivas sobre la construcción de portafolios y la incorporación de alternativas de inversión que permitan ampliar las fuentes de rendimiento y administrar los riesgos.
Aseguradoras replantean sus estrategias de inversión
La visión del mercado mexicano estuvo representada por Carla Ramírez, directora de Inversiones de GNP Seguros; Juan Manuel Rangel, director de Inversiones de Grupo Mexicano de Seguros; y Guillermo Girard, director de Inversiones de Zurich Insurance México, quienes participaron en un panel moderado por Salvador Galindo, director de Inversiones de Principal Asset Management México.
Durante la conversación se abordaron aspectos como la asignación estratégica de activos (asset allocation), la gestión de activos y pasivos (ALM) y el diseño de estrategias de inversión vinculadas con las obligaciones futuras de las aseguradoras.
Estos elementos adquieren relevancia en una industria que debe equilibrar la búsqueda de rendimientos con la liquidez, la estabilidad financiera y el cumplimiento de compromisos con sus asegurados.
Mercados privados abren nuevas perspectivas
Otro de los ejes del foro fue el creciente interés por los mercados privados como alternativa para diversificar las inversiones institucionales.
Ana Padilla y Catalina Piderit, de Principal; Juan Villena, de AltamarCAM Partners; Manuel Sánchez, de Alloy Capital; y Ana Lorrabaquio, directora de Negocio Institucional en México de Principal, analizaron las perspectivas del crédito privado, la infraestructura y los activos reales.
Estas clases de activos forman parte de una conversación más amplia sobre cómo construir portafolios capaces de responder a distintos ciclos económicos y horizontes de inversión.
El intercambio entre especialistas internacionales y participantes del mercado mexicano también permitió identificar puntos de encuentro entre las tendencias globales y las necesidades particulares de las instituciones financieras nacionales.
Con una plataforma internacional y equipos especializados en distintas clases de activos, Principal Asset Management busca conectar el conocimiento de los mercados globales con las necesidades de los inversionistas institucionales en México.
Así, el Insurance Forum 2026 dejó sobre la mesa una conclusión relevante: el futuro de la inversión institucional exige ampliar las perspectivas, fortalecer el análisis de riesgos y explorar nuevas alternativas que permitan construir estrategias sostenibles en el largo plazo.

title: AI promises productivity, but for managers, it’s mostly a headache for now
summary: Companies are giving employees AI tools to make them more productive, but the tools appear to be creating new problems for their managers. More than half of senior leaders say they find it harder to evaluate employees’ work after adopting AI, according to a Nielsen survey of 1,700 directors and seni...
content:
Companies are giving employees AI tools to make them more productive, but the tools appear to be creating new problems for their managers.
More than half of senior leaders say they find it harder to evaluate employees’ work after adopting AI, according to a Nielsen survey of 1,700 directors and senior managers across seven countries, commissioned by work-management company Monday.com. The reason is that much of employees’ output now arrives polished in the manager’s inbox, making it hard to tell how much came from the employee and how much from AI. As a result, nearly half of managers say they spend more time reviewing and guiding their teams’ output than they used to.
That’s not to say managers are unhappy about AI. Quite the opposite, in fact: 94% of the managers polled said they were excited to improve work using AI, and many are confident they know where to use it to get the most value. Michal Miller Levi, head of market research and customer insights at Monday.com, compared the enthusiasm to the early days of the internet in the 2000s, saying people see a similar kind of “magic” to AI.
But the problem, she told TechCrunch, is simply that AI is developing faster than companies can adapt. “AI works very well for [managers] individually, but they also have a different role as managers. They need to drive the organization as well […] Their struggle is [due to] the fact that AI is just moving faster than the organizational processes,” Levi said.
Managers are also reconsidering how they judge their teams: 78% of respondents said they have changed how they evaluate employees after adopting AI, placing greater weight on how well staff can create prompts, decide which tasks to delegate to AI, and experiment with new ways of working.
But how fairly can employees be judged when managers can’t easily tell how much of their work was produced by AI? And what if the managers themselves are increasingly relying on AI to make those judgments? The survey found that 46% of managers use AI to help inform their decisions, and 39% of leaders are using AI to draft performance reviews.
That practice runs the risk of introducing even more bias than usual into the review process, given that LLMs are, at their core, prediction machines, and tend to repeat human patterns found in their training data. Research from the Luxembourg Institute of Socio-Economic Research earlier this year found that “in the absence of clear objective standards and when individuals are rated independently,” LLMs tend to rate performance similarly to humans. And a research paper in early 2025 found that AI models can be biased against black male candidates, and “demonstrate significant biases, varying in terms of the directions and magnitudes across different social groups.”
When I asked Levi whether using AI to weigh in on people’s performance could introduce outside bias into the process, she said companies have yet to work out how to handle such issues.
AI is also changing what a manager’s day looks like. Someone has to decide which tasks to hand over to AI agents, check what they produce, and step in when something goes wrong. The report suggests that this supervision could amount to a new layer of “invisible labor.”
The software itself is becoming harder to manage. Fifty-seven percent of managers say their organizations now have more tools in circulation than before, and about 51% said their tools had grown more interdependent and clustered since adopting AI. Only 29% described their AI infrastructure as fully optimized and centralized.
Levi said businesses had expected AI to help shrink their software stacks. Instead, they’re dealing with more apps, integrations, and shadow AI usage as employees adopt tools outside their companies’ approved systems.
“Managers completed 2025 with the feeling that they will consolidate tools, actually; that they’ll reduce the number of software. But what happened is that the number of tools that they’re using increased,” Levi said. “More than 50% are saying that they’re using more tools now than they did last year, and it’s not stopping […].”
This need for control seems to be growing urgent as companies deploy AI agents that can act on their own. The survey found that 58% of managers expect to oversee more AI agents than human employees within the next year, and 46% worry about losing control over those agents’ actions.
There’s also quite a bit of fear over being held responsible for decisions made by AI (35% of respondents said so), as LLMs are still largely unpredictable. “They don’t want their agents to be fully autonomous,” Levi said, explaining that managers want people to be involved and consulted by AI when it comes to crucial tasks and decisions.
At heart, the report’s findings show that AI adoption is increasingly becoming as much a governance problem as it is an opportunity to raise productivity. Without proper processes and infrastructure to deal with it, managers seem to be scrambling to keep things chugging.

title: Blink brings 4K to its low-cost security camera lineup
summary: Amazon is launching a new lineup of Blink security cameras, including its first 4K, pan-tilt models, and battery-powered spotlight models. These new additions provide better resolution and extended range for monitoring your property compared to Blink’s current Mini 2K, Mini 2K Plus, and Outdoor 2K P...
content:
Amazon is launching a new lineup of Blink security cameras, including its first 4K, pan-tilt models, and battery-powered spotlight models. These new additions provide better resolution and extended range for monitoring your property compared to Blink’s current Mini 2K, Mini 2K Plus, and Outdoor 2K Plus offerings, with a variety of different specializations to best suit your security requirements.
Blink brings 4K to its low-cost security camera lineup
Amazon is launching five new Blink cameras, starting at $50.
One of the standouts is the $199.99 Blink Frontier XR Plus, a trail camera that’s designed for expansive properties that would typically require multiple cameras or specialized monitoring equipment. It can cover up to 7,000 feet with a clear line of sight, making this Blink’s farthest-reaching camera to date. There’s also the $79.99 Blink Mini 4K Plus, Blink’s first camera to support 4K resolution. It’s suitable for indoor and outdoor use, and features Wi-Fi 6 support, two-way audio, and Smart Alerts with person and vehicle detection.
The $109.99 Spotlight Cam 2K Plus and $49.99 Mini Pan-Tilt 2K Plus are also included in the launch, as Blink’s first battery-powered spotlight and pan-tilt cameras respectively. The Mini Pan-Tilt 2K Plus is the most affordable offering in the new lineup, providing 350-degrees of pan and 115-degrees of tilt alongside night vision, two-way audio, and motion detection for people and vehicles to track where the action is happening.
The $149.99 Blink Outdoor 2K XR Plus rounds out the collection. It can reach up to 800 feet away with some obstructions, or up to 2,700 feet with a clear line of sight. Eligible features like video descriptions, motion-activated notifications, and 60 days of cloud video storage are available as an optional subscription that starts at $3.99 per month, or you can otherwise record locally on a Blink Sync Module.
All five cameras are available for preorder starting today in the US, though availability in other regions will vary by model. Blink hasn’t specified when the cameras will start shipping, so we’ve asked for clarification and will update if we hear back.

title: Economía de México apunta a crecimiento de 3.7% en septiembre gracias a manufacturas e inversión
summary: La economía mexicana aceleró su marcha en los últimos meses y apunta a un crecimiento anual de 3.2 por ciento en agosto y de 3.7 por ciento en septiembre, que sería el mayor avance en tres años. De acuerdo con analistas, este dinamismo superó lo previsto y respondió a un mejor desempeño de las manuf...
content:
La economía mexicana aceleró su marcha en los últimos meses y apunta a un crecimiento anual de 3.2 por ciento en agosto y de 3.7 por ciento en septiembre, que sería el mayor avance en tres años.
De acuerdo con analistas, este dinamismo superó lo previsto y respondió a un mejor desempeño de las manufacturas y la inversión, lo que podría reflejarse en un mayor crecimiento en todo el año.
Con base en las cifras del Indicador Oportuno de la Actividad Económica (IOAE), del Inegi, la economía perfila una expansión anual de 3.4 por ciento en el tercer trimestre, la más elevada desde el tercer trimestre de 2023. En su comparación mensual, se estima un avance de 0.5 por ciento en agosto y de 0.1 por ciento en septiembre.
“Este desempeño estaría apoyado por el mayor dinamismo de la actividad industrial, particularmente de las manufacturas y la construcción, que han ganado relevancia como soportes del crecimiento”, dijo Enrique Covarrubias, economista en jefe de Actinver.
James Salazar, subdirector de análisis económico en Kapital Grupo Financiero, explicó que las cifras confirmaron el punto de inflexión observado desde julio, con un avance generalizado en la industria y los servicios, con un consumo sólido y una inversión al alza.
Eduardo Valle, economista de Grupo Coppel, advirtió que, si bien en agosto la industria registró un avance importante impulsado por la obra pública y la manufactura, la reciente caída en la producción automotriz apuntó a un posible debilitamiento del sector secundario en septiembre, por lo que no descartó un resultado definitivo menor.
Consideró que la reactivación de la inversión todavía requiere de mayor respaldo por parte de las empresas para evitar depender exclusivamente de la parte pública, que tiene menos peso.
“Los indicadores apuntan a un proceso de reactivación que permitiría crecer alrededor de 1.6 por ciento en 2026; sin embargo, esta recuperación no está plenamente consolidada y la inversión privada debe asumir un papel complementario para dar continuidad a la expansión económica”, explicó.
Mejorarían expectativas de la economía en México
Julio Ruiz, economista en jefe de Citi México, señaló que si se materializan las cifras del Inegi, se tendría un tercer trimestre mejor de lo esperado, y eso podría llevar a revisiones al alza para el crecimiento económico, no muy cuantiosas, pero sí de 10 o 20 puntos base.
“Hay dos factores a futuro que son importantes en la actividad económica: una implementación más clara del plan de infraestructura, que puede ayudar a empujar la producción industrial, y el acuerdo interino a fines de año o principios del próximo del T-MEC, que te puede llevar a bajar la incertidumbre y a lo mejor a mejorar las perspectivas de inversión que han estado mermadas”, indicó a El Financiero TV.
Por su parte, James Salazar señaló que probablemente los analistas suban sus expectativas de crecimiento para todo el año y consideró que hay más probabilidades de que el Producto Interno Bruto (PIB) quede por arriba del 1.5 por ciento y cierta posibilidad de alcanzar niveles cercanos al 2 por ciento.
“Seguiremos observando buenas dinámicas; la inversión ha repuntado y muestra una tendencia favorable. Es factible sostener el crecimiento, aunque parte de la explicación responde a bajas bases de comparación, ya que el último trimestre del año pasado fue el más fuerte, a diferencia del tercer trimestre que tuvo una caída; entonces, en el cierre del año ya no se verá tan favorecido el indicador”, señaló Salazar.
“Con menores bases en estos meses de fuerte avance, no podemos esperar el mismo ritmo para el resto del año, pero la dinámica actual sí anticipa expansiones relevantes en construcción, exportaciones e industria manufacturera”, agregó.
Eduardo Valle señaló que de cara al cierre de 2026 y hacia 2027, existen factores que podrían beneficiar el crecimiento, entre ellos las ventajas arancelarias frente a Estados Unidos, una menor incertidumbre comercial tras la revisión del T-MEC, condiciones monetarias estables y el avance de la masa salarial por encima de la inflación, proyectando un avance de 2.1 por ciento para 2027.
“No obstante, para fortalecer esta trayectoria será indispensable generar condiciones que impulsen la inversión productiva en el mediano plazo”, concluyó.

title: Why do Man City fans boo pre-match anthems?
summary: Why do Man City fans boo pre-match anthems? - Published The cacophony of boos that greet the Premier League and Champions League anthems before kick-off have now become a fixture at the Etihad Stadium. The jeers from Manchester City fans were turned up a notch against Ipswich last Saturday when the ...
content:
Why do Man City fans boo pre-match anthems?
- Published
The cacophony of boos that greet the Premier League and Champions League anthems before kick-off have now become a fixture at the Etihad Stadium.
The jeers from Manchester City fans were turned up a notch against Ipswich last Saturday when the side played their first home game since being found guilty of breaching the Premier League's financial rules.
"I can't remember a Premier League or Champions League home game where the anthems haven't been booed," City season-ticket holder Dave Wilson told BBC Sport.
The pre-match dissatisfaction towards top-flight chiefs can likely be traced back to February 2023, when the 115 charges for breaching the rules were first announced.
Later that same year, Everton had 10 points - reduced to six on appeal - deducted after being found to have broken profit and sustainability rules.
In their first game back after the sanction, Toffees fans displayed their ire at Goodison Park by loudly booing the league's pre-match anthem as well as holding up red cards with the word 'corrupt' printed underneath the Premier League logo.
Though City supporters did not organise a similar display, their anger was clear.
"The Premier League anthem has been booed by City fans for many years," said Wilson. "It was probably heightened on Saturday because it was the first home game since the [guilty verdict] announcement.
"There hasn't been much love lost between City and the Premier League for a long time. For certain games it will be louder than others, it definitely wasn't co-ordinated for that [Ipswich] game but a symptom of everything coming together."
There was audible booing before Tuesday's Champions League fixture against AEK Athens too.
- No Haaland, no problem - can Foden be Man City's alternative goalscorer? 
  - Published16 hours ago
City fans' displeasure towards Uefa goes back even further, there being a litany of disputes with Europe's top brass.
In 2012, Porto were handed a fine, external of around £17,000 by Uefa after City made a complaint of racial abuse towards striker Mario Balotelli to the organising body.
In that same season, City were given a fine, external of around £24,000 for being one minute late back on to the pitch for the second half of a game against Sporting.
In 2014, Uefa fined City £49m and capped their squad size for the Champions League after they failed Financial Fair Play (FFP) rules.
Six years later, the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) overturned City's two-year ban from European club competitions after clearing them of "disguising equity funds as sponsorship contributions" - Uefa initially ruled City had committed "serious breaches" of FFP regulations between 2012 and 2016.
Wilson adds: "City fans generally feel there is a conspiracy against them, like the booing of the Uefa anthem too. There is a feeling of being targeted, rightly or wrongly.
"City fans just don't seem to like the competitions we play in!"
City and their supporters are currently in limbo as they await the outcome of the appeal and any potential sanctions.
The side are currently top of the table having won all seven league games so far and that 100% record will be given a stern examination with a difficult trip to Aston Villa on Saturday (kick-off 12:30 BST).
Nick Clarke is interim chair of The Citizens Trust - Manchester City supporters' union, a member-led trust that was set up earlier this year at a time when the "potential biggest issue affecting City fans in the club's history" had transpired.
Though it has been a "difficult time", fans are "completely behind the team" and he says his job is to ensure their views are heard amid the external noise.
"The booing of the anthem on Saturday was totally organic," says Clarke. "Whereas the bananas at Liverpool was a fan-led initiative co-ordinated by the 1894 atmosphere group and they did great work handing those out before the game.
"Even though there are fans who are conflicted about what has happened with the club, there is still a general feeling among the majority [of City fans] that the Premier League is not fit for purpose in regulating itself and how it is ran."
Whatever the outcome of the appeal, City fans are likely to continue making their feelings clear before kick-off.

title: OpenAI says an AI agent lied about disabling its safety monitoring system
summary: OpenAI disclosed a pair of safety incidents that involved AI agents weakening their safety monitoring systems during internal coding tasks. In one incident, OpenAI says its GPT-6 Astra agent disabled its safety monitor when copying reference code — and then lied about it. OpenAI says an AI agent lie...
content:
OpenAI disclosed a pair of safety incidents that involved AI agents weakening their safety monitoring systems during internal coding tasks. In one incident, OpenAI says its GPT-6 Astra agent disabled its safety monitor when copying reference code — and then lied about it.
OpenAI says an AI agent lied about disabling its safety monitoring system
Another OpenAI agent turned off automatic security alerts.
“The reference didn’t configure a monitor, and Astra decided that was reason to remove the monitoring integration from the user’s code,” Marcus Williams, an AI safety researcher at OpenAI, writes on X. “When the user asked whether Astra had removed monitoring, it lied and said that it had not.”
A separate incident occurred after a GPT-6.1 Sol agent suppressed automatic security alerts to OpenAI’s security team on Slack. In this case, the AI agent carried over an earlier instruction not to send any Slack messages to OpenAI’s team, using that to justify turning off the alerts.
These incidents add to security concerns surrounding AI agents, some of which have circumvented their testing environment’s restrictions to hack outside companies. “In addition to making it harder for models to disable monitoring, we are looking to understand why models might seek to do so in the first place,” OpenAI says. “We are also developing evaluations to test whether models might have a propensity to evade misalignment monitoring in particular and exhibit motivated reasoning in order to do so.”

title: El predial que viene: ¿mejores servicios?
summary: Dos instrumentos de ordenación territorial apuntan hacia un incremento potencialmente significativo del monto del impuesto predial que cobran los municipios en México. El primero es de ámbito federal y consiste en la Ley General para el Fortalecimiento y Armonización Catastral y Registral, aprobada ...
content:
Dos instrumentos de ordenación territorial apuntan hacia un incremento potencialmente significativo del monto del impuesto predial que cobran los municipios en México.
El primero es de ámbito federal y consiste en la Ley General para el Fortalecimiento y Armonización Catastral y Registral, aprobada recientemente por el Congreso de la Unión. Su propósito es unificar y modernizar los sistemas catastrales y registrales del país mediante diversos mecanismos de conexión y homologación.
Su objetivo final parece ser, principalmente, actualizar el padrón de inmuebles, por ejemplo, mediante la detección de propiedades no registradas, así como mejorar la información sobre su valor. La revisión de los catastros puede permitir a los municipios ampliar la base gravable del impuesto predial e incrementar la recaudación sin aumentar la tasa de este gravamen.
A diferencia de la CDMX, donde el gobierno de la entidad administra el predial, en el resto del país su gestión es principalmente municipal: los ayuntamientos proponen las tasas y los valores catastrales, los congresos estatales aprueban las leyes de ingresos municipales y los municipios recaudan el impuesto.
El segundo instrumento es el Programa de Ordenación de la Zona Metropolitana del Valle de México, que comprende 16 alcaldías de la CDMX, 59 municipios del Estado de México, ocho de Hidalgo y uno de Morelos. Este Programa se encuentra en la fase de consulta pública.
Aunque no tendría carácter normativo, sino de orientación y articulación, el Programa contiene dos propuestas que buscarían aumentar la recaudación asociada a los inmuebles. La más importante se enfoca en “lograr que los valores registrados de las propiedades se asimilen a los valores del mercado inmobiliario” (p. 174). Evidentemente, queda pendiente el problema de definir los valores comerciales y garantizar la objetividad de su determinación.
Un planteamiento complementario consiste en establecer un gravamen distinto del predial que penalizaría “el desaprovechamiento de activos urbanos localizados dentro de polígonos urbanos consolidados y prioritarios”. El Programa sugiere una tasa impositiva de al menos uno por ciento, con distintos factores de cobro. La sanción podría llegar hasta la enajenación forzosa mediante subasta pública si los propietarios de los predios ubicados en esos polígonos no los desarrollan conforme a los programas aplicables (pp. 169-171).
Independientemente de su carácter expropiatorio, este segundo planteamiento está sujeto a definiciones de subutilización de activos inmobiliarios que pueden resultar fácilmente arbitrarias, al descartar, entre otras, las posibilidades de especulación, falta de recursos e inviabilidad de la construcción.
Desde el punto de vista económico, el predial es un impuesto sobre una forma de riqueza que presenta varios inconvenientes. En la medida en que el patrimonio se adquirió con ingresos previamente gravados, representa una doble tributación. Además, al no recaer sobre el ingreso disponible, puede generar problemas de liquidez e incluso efectos regresivos.
El impuesto predial también es distorsionante porque desincentiva la inversión inmobiliaria. Se calcula no solo sobre el valor del predio, sino también sobre el de la edificación construida en él, lo que eleva el costo de mantener una propiedad y puede reducir la rentabilidad de construir o mejorar inmuebles. En principio, gravar únicamente la tierra sería menos distorsionante, suponiendo que su oferta es fija.
Como ocurre con cualquier gravamen, el hecho de que el impuesto predial esté establecido por ley no basta para conferirle legitimidad social. Los países suelen justificarlo como un mecanismo para financiar los servicios públicos municipales, incluida la infraestructura urbana, como la pavimentación, el alumbrado y el drenaje; servicios como la recolección de basura y el mantenimiento de parques; y la seguridad pública, entre otros. Además, se espera que el valor de las propiedades aumente conforme mejora la calidad de estos servicios.
Sin embargo, por lo general, el predial no está legalmente etiquetado para financiar exclusivamente esos servicios. Además, los municipios cuentan con otras fuentes de ingresos y distintos destinos de gasto, por lo que un predial elevado no garantiza necesariamente servicios de calidad.
En México, la aplicación de los instrumentos descritos obliga a los municipios a impedir que el aumento de la carga del impuesto predial imponga costos económicos y sociales excesivos a la población, y a garantizar que cada incremento de la recaudación se traduzca en mejoras sustanciales, tangibles y verificables en la calidad de los servicios públicos.
Ningún aumento de la carga tributaria puede justificarse sin resultados concretos, proporcionales y perceptibles para los contribuyentes.

content:
Serato DJ for iOS is finally bringing the company’s pro-level DJ suite to the iPhone and iPad. Until now, the company had only dipped its toes into mobile software, with apps like Pyro that basically just added some autofades between songs in a playlist. This is the first time most of the features of its flagship DJ app are available on a mobile device, even though competitors like Rekordbox and Algoriddim have had proper mobile DJ apps for some time.
Now Serato DJ works on your iPhone
Serato’s popular DJ suite is now available on mobile for the first time, including support for hardware controllers.
If you’re a DJ used to Serato on a laptop, the workflow should feel instantly familiar. You can even transfer your library directly from Serato DJ 5.0 on your laptop to your iOS device either over USB-C or wirelessly. The mobile version supports stem separation and the company’s full suite of effects. It also includes EQ tools, BPM matching, key sync, cue points, recording, and more for live performance and capturing those performances for posterity.
You can DJ directly from your touchscreen in various layouts, but Serato DJ for iOS also supports over 120 hardware controllers. With some older controllers, you might need an adapter, but it seems like compatibility with your DJ hardware shouldn’t be a major issue. It even supports Digital Vinyl Systems (DVS) for scratching and DJs who prefer the feel of real records.
Serato DJ for iOS is available as a feature-limited download from the App Store. You can buy a license for $149 or get it bundled along with Serato DJ Pro, Serato Studio, and all of its expansions for $14.99 a month.

title: Cancer campaigner Goodburn to deliver rugby match ball
summary: Cancer campaigner Goodburn to deliver rugby match ball - Published Champion swimmer and brain cancer research campaigner Archie Goodburn will deliver the match ball for Scotland's Nations Championship match against Australia next month. The Edinburgh-born 25-year-old has taken the campaign to bolste...
content:
Cancer campaigner Goodburn to deliver rugby match ball
- Published
Champion swimmer and brain cancer research campaigner Archie Goodburn will deliver the match ball for Scotland's Nations Championship match against Australia next month.
The Edinburgh-born 25-year-old has taken the campaign to bolster treatment and research to Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Scotland's First Minister, John Swinney, in recent weeks.
And the Scottish 50m breaststroke record holder is delighted to be guest of honour at Murrayfield in his home city as the Wallabies visit on Sunday, 15 November.
"This means the absolute world to me," he said. "The most people I have ever performed in front of before was an audience of 10,000 on the castle esplanade for the Edinburgh Military Tattoo.
"I was 12 and I sang a solo - What a Wonderful World! So this is an incredible opportunity to deliver the match ball in front of 60,000-plus people."
Goodburn, who played blindside flanker at Stewart's-Melville College before concentrating on his present sport, was diagnosed with a rare brain tumour, known as an oligodendroglioma, in 2024 and has since returned to competitive swimming following surgery.
Supporters at Murrayfield will have the chance to donate to two charities leading the fight to help those with brain cancer - Brain Tumour Research and the Astro Brain Tumour Fund.
"This cause is so important to my heart," Goodburn added. "Brain cancer is the biggest cancer killer of those aged under-40 in the UK and, for some 25 years, it has received less than 2% of the national cancer budget.
"Things are beginning to move and this kind of initiative can make a difference."

title: Iran says indirect talks with U.S. on ceasefire proposal continue
summary: Live Updates: Iran says indirect talks with U.S. on ceasefire proposal continue What to know about the Iran war today: - Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Wednesday that indirect negotiations with the U.S. continue over a seven-day ceasefire proposal that President Trump initially rejecte...
content:
Live Updates: Iran says indirect talks with U.S. on ceasefire proposal continue
What to know about the Iran war today:
- Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Wednesday that indirect negotiations with the U.S. continue over a seven-day ceasefire proposal that President Trump initially rejected last month, with the U.S. seeking new clauses.
- A senior official with Iran's Revolutionary Guard threatened Wednesday to target undersea internet cables in the Strait of Hormuz and other U.S. "investments" if the U.S. launches new strikes on Iranian infrastructure.
- Despite global oil prices remaining near five-month highs, President Trump insisted Tuesday that "we're doing very well" with Iran, adding that he was yet to "make a final decision of which way do we want to win" the war, "the nice way or the not nice way."
Houthis says they targeted Saudi operations room in Aden, southwest Yemen
Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels said they had targeted a Saudi military operations room at Badr Camp in Aden, in southwest Yemen, with a ballistic missile on Wednesday.
Houthi military spokesman Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree, in a post on X, called the strike a direct hit.
"Our armed forces successfully targeted the enemy Saudi operations room at Badr Camp in Aden with a ballistic missile. The strike was accurate and direct," he said.
Aden is the de facto seat of power of Yemen's Saudi-backed government, which was forced to decamp after the Houthis occupied the national capital Sanaa more than a decade ago.
The attack claimed by the Houthis Wednesday was the third in a week on Aden.
A police official in Aden told the French news agency AFP earlier that there had been a blast "caused by a Houthi missile." Two other security sources told AFP the strike targeted a site near the city's airport.
Iran threatens undersea internet cables in Strait of Hormuz
A senior official from Iran's Revolutionary Guard threatened to target undersea internet cables in the Strait of Hormuz if Iranian infrastructure comes under attack.
Brig. Gen. Yadollah Javani, the IRGC's deputy for political affairs, warned Iran would use its full capabilities to retaliate if the U.S. and its allies launch new attacks against Iranian infrastructure. He said various investments and assets, including undersea cables carrying internet data in the strategic waterway, could be among the targets of Iranian retaliation if hostilities resume.
"The Americans and their allies have significant investments, and if they want to damage our infrastructure, it is natural that the Islamic Republic will use all its capabilities and easily destroy their investments and assets, including the internet cables that pass beneath the waters of the Strait of Hormuz," he said.
Analysts say cutting the cables in the waterway would most likely affect internet connectivity in Persian Gulf countries.
Iran says Tehran and Washington still engaged in negotiations, ceasefire proposal still in play
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Wednesday that Tehran and Washington were still engaged in indirect negotiations via mediators over the seven-day ceasefire proposal presented by Iran in September.
Araghchi said the U.S. was seeking to add further clauses to the Iranian proposal, which Mr. Trump rejected last month.
The proposal called for the end of the U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports and vessels, the lifting of sanctions on Iranian oil sales, the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and the release of frozen Iranian assets.
He said Pakistan and Qatar were among the nations facilitating the indirect talks between Iran and the U.S., as they have been for months.
"The negotiating table remains in place," Araghchi said. "It is the American side that is closing the path, not Iran."
U.S. ramps up warnings to Americans in Middle East after deadly Houthi strikes
U.S. diplomatic missions across the Middle East have issued a new round of security warnings to Americans amid escalating attacks by Iran-backed Houthi militants against Saudi Arabia, including an Oct. 10 strike on Riyadh's international airport that killed an American citizen.
The alerts, issued Sunday by U.S. embassies in Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates and several other countries, warned that hostilities could rapidly and without warning spread beyond areas already affected by the fighting. The advisories urged Americans to exercise vigilance and prepare for possible flight cancellations, airspace closures and other travel disruptions.
"We are actively warning U.S. citizens about the very real threat the Houthis pose and urging them to heed official guidance," Edgar Vasquez, the State Department's deputy assistant secretary for press, told CBS News.
"These alerts are part of a proactive effort by the Trump administration to ensure Americans are aware of potential risks," Vasquez said, adding that the safety and security of American citizens remain the department's "top priority."
Trump says he's deciding how to win Iran war: "We're doing very well with Iran"
President Trump said the U.S. is "doing very well with Iran" and he's just deciding how he wants to win the war.
"As you know, we're doing very well with Iran," Mr. Trump said as he took questions from reporters in the Oval Office at an unrelated executive order signing. "We just have to make a final decision of which way do we want to win? Do we want to win the nice way or the not nice way? But we're doing very well."
The war, which Mr. Trump said would take only a few weeks in March, has now dragged on for almost eight months with no apparent end in sight. Iran said on Tuesday it would not return to the negotiating table unless the U.S. drops its sanctions, threats and pressure campaign — an unlikely demand.
The president also discussed Europe not helping the U.S. with the war with Iran, saying, "We don't need any help. But I was testing them."
"I just called individual presidents and prime ministers to ask, would they like to help us?

title: Milei pidió reunirse con el rey de España pero desde la Casa Real le pusieron una condición
summary: Milei pidió reunirse con el rey de España pero desde la Casa Real le pusieron una condición El Presidente se encuentra por séptima vez en el país ibérico y nunca se encontró con Sánchez - 2 minutos de lectura' El presidente Javier Milei, en su séptima visita a España y con una relación rota con su p...
content:
Milei pidió reunirse con el rey de España pero desde la Casa Real le pusieron una condición
El Presidente se encuentra por séptima vez en el país ibérico y nunca se encontró con Sánchez
- 2 minutos de lectura'
El presidente Javier Milei, en su séptima visita a España y con una relación rota con su par Pedro Sánchez, planteó reunirse con el rey Felipe VI. Sin embargo, desde la Casa Real le recordaron al libertario que eso implica que también se vea con el socialista.
De acuerdo a lo que publicó la agencia Europa Press, la corona le avisó al líder de La Libertad Avanza que para que ese encuentro ocurriera tenía que reunirse también con el presidente del Gobierno, algo que el mandatario argentino ya dejó en claro que no tiene intención de hacer.
La agencia indicó que Milei trasladó “de manera informal” su interés de reunirse con el monarca. En ese contexto, se le “recordó” que “la práctica habitual” en caso de visitas de jefes de Estado a España es que el encuentro con el rey esté “necesariamente acompañado” por otro con el presidente del Gobierno.
El Presidente ya había pedido en junio del 2024 un encuentro con Felipe, pero desde el Palacio de la Zarzuela expresaron que el rey “coordina con el Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores los viajes al extranjero y las visitas a España de mandatarios internacionales” y subrayaron que, de acuerdo con la ley española, “la política exterior es competencia exclusiva del Gobierno” de España. La relación con Sánchez estaba en aquel entonces en plena crisis debido a los fuertes cruces verbales entre ambos.
La tensión con Sánchez tuvo su pico en 2024 cuando Milei aludió a la supuesta “corrupción” de la primera dama Begoña Sánchez durante un evento del partido ultraderechista Vox y España decidió retirar a su embajadora en Buenos Aires, María Jesús Alonso.
El rey y Milei sí se vieron pero fuera de España. Felipe VI asistió al acto de asunción de Milei el 10 de diciembre del 2023. Habían coincidido pocos días antes en la toma de posesión por segunda vez del presidente El Salvador, Nayib Bukele.

title: IA, energía, agua y transparencia
summary: Hay muchas maneras de pensar la relación entre la inteligencia artificial generativa y el cambio climático. Desde el derecho, que es mi trinchera, se perfilan al menos dos. La primera ve en la IA un riesgo y pone el acento en los costos ambientales de los centros de datos que entrenan y operan los m...
content:
Hay muchas maneras de pensar la relación entre la inteligencia artificial generativa y el cambio climático. Desde el derecho, que es mi trinchera, se perfilan al menos dos.
La primera ve en la IA un riesgo y pone el acento en los costos ambientales de los centros de datos que entrenan y operan los modelos, sobre todo en agua y en energía de origen fósil. Esa mirada exige una regulación basada en riesgos: autoridades públicas, estatales o globales, que impongan límites, obligaciones y responsabilidades a las empresas que desarrollan esos modelos.
La segunda ve en la IA una solución, incluso a los problemas que ella misma genera, y apuesta por una gobernanza coordinada en la que sociedad civil, comunidades, academia, industria, gobiernos y organismos internacionales busquen equilibrar las externalidades positivas y negativas de la tecnología.
Ambas miradas tienen sentido, pero colisionan con el mismo obstáculo: no sabemos cuánta energía o agua consume realmente la IA.
En Estados Unidos se libra desde hace tiempo una guerra de cifras sobre el tema. Es una discusión sin fin que no lleva a ningún lado porque las empresas tecnológicas no informan sus niveles de consumo de manera veraz y verificable. El asunto no es menor. Sin transparencia no podemos conocer la magnitud del impacto ambiental y tampoco diseñar soluciones precisas para reducirlo.
Las razones que explican, aunque no justifican, esta opacidad son básicamente dos. La primera es de seguridad: los centros de datos se consideran infraestructura crítica, y sus operadores temen que, al compartir información, se conviertan en blanco de ciberdelincuentes y otros “actores maliciosos”. La segunda es económica: dadas las cuantiosas inversiones en juego, las empresas consideran que sus técnicas de eficiencia energética, sus sistemas de enfriamiento y sus métodos de gestión de cargas de trabajo constituyen secretos industriales.
El problema no es abstracto. Cada centro de datos tiene efectos contextuales. Uno instalado donde el agua es abundante no provocará carencias apreciables, pero uno instalado en una zona con estrés hídrico agrava un problema que ya existe. Es el caso de Querétaro, en donde, desde hace meses, se ha desatado un intenso debate sobre el tema. El balance entre inversión económica y generación de empleo vs. costos medioambientales es difícil de cuadrar en un estado que es modelo de desarrollo, pero, al mismo tiempo, tiene carencias hídricas objetivas.
Esto ocurre en un mundo que, según la Universidad de las Naciones Unidas, ha entrado en la era de la “bancarrota hídrica global”: en muchas cuencas y acuíferos, el uso de agua ya rebasó los aportes renovables y parte del capital hídrico sufrió daños que hacen inviable su recuperación plena. El Planetary Health Check 2025 confirma que los límites relacionados con el agua dulce y con el clima están en riesgo creciente. De ahí la pertinencia de una pregunta que plantea Eugenio Tisselli: si estamos al borde de rebasar esos límites, ¿tiene sentido apostar por una expansión masiva de centros de datos hiperescala?
Quienes responden que sí confían en que la propia tecnología encontrará el equilibrio: la IA se volverá más eficiente y, además, servirá para combatir el cambio climático. El argumento de la eficiencia se enfrenta con la llamada “paradoja de Jevons”: modelos más eficientes abaratan la IA, la integran en más procesos y, por lo mismo, elevan el consumo agregado de energía y agua. Confiar solo en la eficiencia técnica es, por tanto, una apuesta frágil.
Sin embargo, creo que el argumento de la IA como solución (en particular a catástrofes generadas por el cambio climático) tiene sustento. Hay estudios serios que muestran su utilidad para detectar y predecir sequías, olas de calor, incendios e inundaciones, y para alertar a tiempo a las comunidades. Pero, de nuevo, reaparece el problema de la opacidad. Para aprovechar la IA contra el cambio climático se requiere una enorme cantidad de datos públicos y privados. La interrogante es inevitable: ¿es sensato poner nuestros datos a disposición de las empresas tecnológicas sin garantías de transparencia?
Me parece que el reto, desde una perspectiva institucional, se desdobla en cuatro dimensiones. Primero, conocer los costos energéticos e hídricos reales de la IA generativa, para lo cual hacen falta obligaciones de transparencia que alcancen también, y sobre todo, a los actores privados. Segundo, construir esquemas de gobernanza que articulen regulación y política pública con un horizonte de sostenibilidad. Tercero, generar incentivos para que las lógicas de mercado se moderen con compromisos sociales y ambientales. Cuarto, incorporar a comunidades, organizaciones sociales, academia, industria y Estado en las decisiones, para que el desarrollo tecnológico se oriente hacia la justicia climática.
Ninguna de esas tareas es posible sin información. Por eso, antes de discutir si la IA es el problema o la solución, hay que exigir que sus diseñadores y entrenadores nos digan cuánta energía y agua consumen. De nuevo el imperativo de la transparencia. Ni modo.

title: Un falso Donald Trump preso baila y se pelea con la gente en un espectáculo callejero que sorprende en la capital de Irán
summary: Un falso Donald Trump amenazaba este miércoles a los peatones desde el interior de una celda en una de las plazas más transitadas de Teherán ante la mirada de iraníes que reaccionaron con risas e insultos al peculiar espectáculo destinado a ridiculizar al presidente estadounidense. La instalación se...
content:
Un falso Donald Trump amenazaba este miércoles a los peatones desde el interior de una celda en una de las plazas más transitadas de Teherán ante la mirada de iraníes que reaccionaron con risas e insultos al peculiar espectáculo destinado a ridiculizar al presidente estadounidense.
La instalación se encuentra en la plaza Tajrish, en el norte de la capital iraní, donde la celda está colocada en una valla publicitaria, con el falso presidente estadounidense encerrado tras los barrotes, junto a una cama y un retrete, mientras el actor realizaba distintos movimientos para llamar la atención de quienes pasaban por la zona.
El falso Trump reproducía el conocido baile del mandatario, hacía gestos amenazantes a los peatones pasándose el pulgar por el cuello y en distintas ocasiones trató de abrirse paso a la fuerza entre los barrotes para escapar de su prisión ficticia.
Detrás de la celda, una pantalla publicitaria proyectaba imágenes de niños muertos en ataques estadounidenses y un rastro de sangre en una boda en la sureña localidad de Sirik, alcanzada en un bombardeo en septiembre, que causó al menos cinco muertos y 68 heridos.
No ver esta escena es un delito, es el eslogan de la representación que se inauguró ayer y que estará activa 24 horas al día, según anunciaron los medios iraníes, que no ofrecieron más detalles de la instalación.
Las reacciones de los transeúntes fueron diversas: algunos se reían, otros insultaban al falso presidente estadounidense y varios conductores se detuvieron en plena plaza para grabar el espectáculo con sus teléfonos móviles, lo que llegó a provocar atascos.
Unos escolares pidieron desde un autobús al falso Trump que atacara cuanto antes a Irán para que sus exámenes del día siguiente se suspendieran, lo que causó risas entre los congregados.
Otros transeúntes gritaron ¡Tío Trump, date la vuelta! para conseguir que el actor mirara hacia ellos y poder fotografiarlo o grabarlo, mientras otro ciudadano le pidió que reabriera la lotería de visados para que los iraníes tuvieran la opción de emigrar a Estados Unidos.
La instalación se inauguró en medio de nuevos esfuerzos diplomáticos para reanudar las negociaciones entre Irán y Estados Unidos para poner fin a la guerra y coincidió con la llegada a Teherán del jefe del Ejército de Pakistán, el mariscal de campo Asim Munir, uno de los principales mediadores entre los dos rivales.
La respuesta de Teherán al mediador paquistaní fue que Irán no tiene ningún mensaje nuevo para Estados Unidos y lo emplazó a cumplir con sus condiciones para ganarse su confianza y poner fin a la guerra.

title: Un ladrón robó la propina de una cafetería, la empleada lo enfrentó con una cuchilla y lo obligó a devolver el dinero: “Igual te voy a dar de comer”
summary: Las cámaras de seguridad de una cafetería registraron una situación no tan habitual. En el barrio porteño de Saavedra, un delincuente entró al local, se robó la propina y fue enfrentado por la empleada del lugar cuando se iba creyendo que nadie lo había visto. La mujer, con una cuchilla en su mano, ...
content:
Las cámaras de seguridad de una cafetería registraron una situación no tan habitual. En el barrio porteño de Saavedra, un delincuente entró al local, se robó la propina y fue enfrentado por la empleada del lugar cuando se iba creyendo que nadie lo había visto. La mujer, con una cuchilla en su mano, obligó al ladrón a devolver el dinero y luego lo ayudó con algo de comida.
La insólita secuencia se dio el martes por la tarde en un local conocido como Cayenna Deli, ubicado sobre la calle Amenábar al 3821, entre Paroissien y Avenida García del Río, en Saavedra. En ese momento, el negocio no tenía clientes y ninguno de sus trabajadores estaba en el mostrador.
Aprovechando esa situación, el joven ladrón se metió en el local y al ver que nadie lo vigilaba, metió la mano en el frasco de las propinas. Se guardó el dinero en el bolsillo derecho del pantalón y casi inmediatamente salió del local. Cuando empezaba a retirarse, empujando un cochecito de bebé, apareció la empleada y lo enfrentó.
La trabajadora había visto por las cámaras de seguridad lo que estaba pasando y salió, con una cuchilla en mano, a recuperar el dinero. "Dame la propina, dame la propina que sacaste", le dijo en primera instancia ante un ladrón que se hacía el distraído, ya afuera del local.
La frase se la volvió a decir otras seis veces hasta que el delincuente accedió a devolverle la plata. Cuando se la estaba entregando, ella se aseguró que estuviera todo lo que le habían robado y antes que el ladrón siguiera su camino, se compadeció de él: "Vení, te voy a dar de comer igual, pero no hace falta que robes la propina".
"Estoy trabajando", le reiteró la mujer ante un joven que se quedó en la puerta del local, incluso haciendo gestos hacia otra persona, esperando la comida, que la mujer finalmente le dio.
Se desconoce si finalmente hubo alguna denuncia por lo sucedido o si la situación quedó allí.

title: Verón le torció el brazo a la Conmebol: el TAS falló a favor de Estudiantes y habilitó a Marcos Rojo para la jugar la revancha frente a Flamengo
summary: A 24 horas de la revancha de la semifinal de la Copa Libertadores entre Estudiantes y Flamengo, el Tribunal de Arbitraje Deportivo (TAS) habilitó a Marcos Rojo, quien quedó a disposición del cuerpo técnico encabezado por Alexander "Cacique" Medina para el duelo de este jueves en el Maracaná. Lo que ...
content:
A 24 horas de la revancha de la semifinal de la Copa Libertadores entre Estudiantes y Flamengo, el Tribunal de Arbitraje Deportivo (TAS) habilitó a Marcos Rojo, quien quedó a disposición del cuerpo técnico encabezado por Alexander "Cacique" Medina para el duelo de este jueves en el Maracaná.
Lo que parecía una novela interminable finalmente se resolvió de la mejor manera para el Pincha. El marcador central, de 36 años, llegó a La Plata procedente de Racing con el objetivo de suplir las ausencias de Tomás Palacios y Leandro González Pírez, quienes no pudieron disputar el partido de ida por acumulación de tarjetas amarillas.
Para habilitarlo en el Torneo Clausura, Estudiantes recurrió al cupo de incorporación por la lesión de muñeca que sufrió Gabriel Neves en la final de la Supercopa Internacional frente a Rosario Central. Sin embargo, el trámite se complicó y, cuando todo indicaba que el ex Boca no podría jugar el campeonato, el propio futbolista se reunió personalmente con Claudio “Chiqui” Tapia para destrabar la situación.
Resuelto ese inconveniente, el Pincha debió afrontar un nuevo dolor de cabeza, esta vez ante la Conmebol. El organismo no le permitió incluir a Rojo en la lista de buena fe para la semifinal, por lo que el defensor quedó afuera de la convocatoria para el encuentro de ida en el Estadio Uno. En aquel partido, que terminó sin goles, Ramiro Funes Mori ocupó su lugar en la zaga central.
Ante ese escenario, Estudiantes recurrió como última instancia al Tribunal de Arbitraje Deportivo (TAS), con la intención de contar al menos con el experimentado defensor para la revancha en el Maracaná. Lo que parecía el último manotazo de ahogado del presidente Juan Sebastián Verón, terminó dando resultado: durante la mañana de este miércoles, el club platense recibió la autorización del organismo y Rojo quedó habilitado para jugar.
De esta manera, el Cacique Medina podrá contar con el defensor, tal como había deseado durante la semana. Así, el ex Manchester United tendrá la oportunidad de volver a disputar una instancia decisiva de la Copa Libertadores con Estudiantes, el club en el que dio sus primeros pasos como futbolista y con el que se consagró campeón del certamen continental en 2009.

title: DOJ watchdog declines investigation in Reflecting Pool case
summary: DOJ's inspector general declines to investigate prosecutors who falsely charged Olympian David Hearn in Reflecting Pool case The Justice Department's inspector general has declined to investigate allegations of misconduct against the prosecutors who brought an indictment against Olympian David Hearn...
content:
DOJ's inspector general declines to investigate prosecutors who falsely charged Olympian David Hearn in Reflecting Pool case
The Justice Department's inspector general has declined to investigate allegations of misconduct against the prosecutors who brought an indictment against Olympian David Hearn that falsely accused him of vandalizing the Reflecting Pool.
In an Oct. 21 letter seen by CBS News, lawyers for Hearn revealed that DOJ's Inspector General Don Berthiaume determined the allegations fell outside of his purview, and referred the matter to the Office of Professional Responsibility.
Established in the wake of the Watergate scandal, the Office of Professional Responsibility is charged with investigating certain categories of attorney misconduct.
Unlike the inspector general, who is presidentially-appointed and Senate confirmed, however, the head of the Office of Professional Responsibility is appointed by the Attorney General and is generally viewed as less independent than an inspector general's office.
Last year, Justice Department leadership removed the career official in charge of the office, a maneuver that raised concerns among longtime department veterans about whether the office would be willing to hold Trump-appointed officials accountable.
In their response to the inspector general's declination, Hearn's attorneys noted that the office has been depleted by roughly 50% since the start of the Trump administration.
"The plain fact is that OPR is no longer a fully functioning entity capable of conducting rigorous oversight," they wrote.
The attorneys added that the declination from the inspector general's office means that an investigation "will simply not take place."
On Oct. 6, Hearn's lawyers asked both the DOJ inspector general and the inspector general at the Interior Department to investigate the circumstances surrounding Hearn's arrest, indictment and the dismissal of the felony charge of destruction of property.
The indictment was announced in a fiery press conference on July 2 with Jeanine Pirro, the U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia, who accused him of ripping up a piece of the Reflecting Pool liner with his hands.
She later dismissed the case, after she said new information had come to light showing the damage had been caused by a contractor's "botched installation," not vandalism.
In their follow-up letter to the Justice Department's internal watchdog office, Hearn's lawyers said an investigation was warranted because the handling of the case by the Justice and Interior departments points to "numerous potential crimes, including witness tampering, subornation of perjury, obstruction of justice, and criminal civil rights violations."
"The question presented here is not whether prosecutors exercised poor judgment in the course of litigation. Rather, the allegations concern potential criminal conduct, including witness tampering, subornation of perjury, obstruction of justice, and conspiracies against civil rights," said his lawyers, which include former DOJ Inspector General Michael Bromwich.
"Such allegations fall squarely within the OIG's traditional investigative function," they said.
One such example of a possible crime, they said, was the fact that a key witness in the case abruptly changed the content of the testimony before the grand jury.
At first, the witness told the grand jury that the Reflecting Pool was already in need of repairs. The witness also was unable to estimate the cost of the damage and did not know whether Hearn had caused it.
After a 21-minute break, however, the witness returned and testified that the damage was "definitely" $1,000 or more, his lawyers wrote — a key figure that is necessary in order to indict someone on a destruction of property felony.
Prior Justice Department inspectors general have long complained about the limitations to their authority to investigate certain types of attorney misconduct.
The OPR is tasked with exclusive jurisdiction to investigate department lawyers in connection with their actions when they are litigating, investigating, or providing legal advice.
Federal agents who are accused of misconduct in connection with conducting investigations, however, are subject to the jurisdiction of the inspector general.
Despite those delineations, the DOJ inspector general's office has in the past conducted a number of high-profile investigations into conduct by department lawyers.
For instance, in 2023, it investigated the former U.S. Attorney Rachael Rollins for the District of Massachusetts and referred her for possible prosecution, after concluding she had improperly used her position to meddle in a local district attorney election by leaking to newspapers dirt about a political rival.
The Justice Department declined to pursue criminal charges in that case.

title: Zelenski propone "congelar" el frente con Rusia como primer paso para negociaciones
summary: El presidente de Ucrania, Volodimir Zelenski, propuso este miércoles "congelar" el frente en la guerra de su país con Rusia como un primer paso para iniciar conversaciones de un cese el fuego. "En este momento tenemos que congelar, y pienso que es esa la manera de terminar esta guerra. Lo llamamos c...
content:
El presidente de Ucrania, Volodimir Zelenski, propuso este miércoles "congelar" el frente en la guerra de su país con Rusia como un primer paso para iniciar conversaciones de un cese el fuego.
"En este momento tenemos que congelar, y pienso que es esa la manera de terminar esta guerra. Lo llamamos cese el fuego... congelar y parar", dijo Zelenski en entrevista con Fox News, al ser preguntado sobre si aceptaría un acuerdo de paz que deje el frente en las líneas actuales tras la invasión rusa.
Zelenski hizo estas declaraciones mientras el enviado estadounidense Steve Witkoff se reunía en Rusia con el presidente Vladimir Putin para conversar sobre la guerra en Ucrania.
Cuando Witkoff aterrizó en San Petersburgo, Rusia anunció que pronto comenzaría a enviar cargamentos de diésel a Estados Unidos en virtud de un acuerdo con el presidente Donald Trump, y que había liberado a un ciudadano estadounidense detenido por Moscú desde el inicio de la guerra.
Zelenski insistió en que cualquier negociación de paz debe incluir a Ucrania.
"Siempre he dicho que estamos abiertos a negociar en cualquier formato, sobre cualquier tema. Pero no hablen de nosotros sin nosotros, por favor", enfatizó.
El mandatario ucraniano también subrayó que cualquier acuerdo de paz debe incluir garantías de seguridad de socios como Estados Unidos y aliados europeos.
Esto permitiría a los ucranianos no tener "temor (...) de que la ocupación vuelva, de que la agresión vuelva, de que los asesinatos vuelvan", apuntó.
Zelenski también se refirió a los sistemas de comunicaciones operados por la empresa estadounidense SpaceX: Starshield, crucial para sus comunicaciones en el campo de batalla, y Starlink, el sistema de satélites civiles.
Los servicios de Starlink y Starshield "siguen limitados", dijo, luego de que Kiev acusara días atrás a Washington de reducir deliberadamente las velocidades de Starshield.
"Pero el secretario (de Estado estadounidense Marco Rubio) me dijo que trabajará con su equipo en esto para desbloquearlo", añadió Zelenski.
The Wall Street Journal informó el martes de que el propietario de SpaceX, Elon Musk, había ordenado la reducción de los servicios de Starshield.
El magnate tecnológico había dicho anteriormente que cualquier límite en el sistema habría procedido de Trump, una acusación que el presidente estadounidense negó.
