title: Excelencia operativa lleva a Afore XXI Banorte a gestionar 9.4 millones de cuentas adicionales del SAR
summary: La Comisión Nacional del Sistema de Ahorro para el Retiro (CONSAR) designó a XXI Banorte como la nueva Prestadora de Servicios del SAR tras dictaminar que es la Afore con la mejor capacidad operativa, solvencia financiera, servicio al cliente y alcance tecnológico de toda la industria, cualidades qu...
content:
La Comisión Nacional del Sistema de Ahorro para el Retiro (CONSAR) designó a XXI Banorte como la nueva Prestadora de Servicios del SAR tras dictaminar que es la Afore con la mejor capacidad operativa, solvencia financiera, servicio al cliente y alcance tecnológico de toda la industria, cualidades que le permitieron ganar la licitación emitida por la autoridad durante 2026.
Derivado de dicha designación, la Afore recibió 9,417,381 Cuentas Individuales que se encuentran pendientes de ser asignadas o registradas, con un saldo acumulado de más de 121 mil millones de pesos. Con este movimiento, XXI Banorte se convierte en la líder del sector al gestionar la mayor cantidad de cuentas del sistema.
Para escoger al ganador de la licitación, la CONSAR evaluó diversos aspectos operativos y financieros de las Afore, concluyendo que XXI Banorte es la Administradora más eficiente del sector, ya que tiene la infraestructura idónea para un desempeño óptimo, ofrece altos niveles de atención y cuenta con una comisión competitiva para brindar el servicio.
Al respecto, Julio César Cervantes Parra, Presidente de la CONSAR, comentó que “esta gestión permitirá una operación más eficiente y de menor costo para el Sistema. La tasa ofrecida por la Administradora generará ahorros en la prestación del servicio, mientras que su capacidad operativa permitirá atender más de nueve millones de cuentas”.
Sobre el resultado de la licitación, David Razú Aznar, Director General de XXI Banorte, señaló que “la designación representa un voto de confianza en la solidez, experiencia y capacidad operativa de la Afore. Asumimos esta responsabilidad con el compromiso de brindar un servicio eficiente, seguro y de calidad, así como de acompañar a las y los trabajadores para que conozcan su Cuenta Individual, tomen decisiones informadas sobre su futuro y se registren en la Afore Fuerte de México”.
De tal manera, a través de este mecanismo regulado por la CONSAR, XXI Banorte asumirá por los siguientes seis años el control de las Cuentas Individuales que aún no están asignadas o registradas en una Administradora. Cabe señalar que los fondos de dichas cuentas se mantienen en el Banco de México, y que la Afore únicamente gestionará la recepción de sus aportaciones patronales, e implementará estrategias para localizar a los titulares de cada Cuenta Individual, a fin de que puedan registrarse en XXI Banorte, recibir sus Estados de Cuenta Cuatrimestrales y conocer el saldo de su Afore.
Como parte de esta designación, XXI Banorte pone a disposición a su equipo de Asesores Previsionales, quienes podrán resolver las dudas o solicitudes de cada persona interesada en conocer más sobre su Afore. En este sentido, la institución invita a las y los trabajadores que aún no se registran en una Afore a solicitar asesoría y formalizar su registro a través de la aplicación AforeMóvil XXIB, el sitio web www.xxi-banorte.com o vía WhatsApp, escribiendo al número 5520001994.

title: Spotify is busting free of CarPlay with the launch of its first native car app
summary: Spotify announced Wednesday the launch of its next-generation, fully native in-car app, built directly on Google’s Android Automotive operating system. The standalone app, which is launching today in select Audi models, runs directly on the vehicle’s infotainment hardware — eliminating the need for ...
content:
Spotify announced Wednesday the launch of its next-generation, fully native in-car app, built directly on Google’s Android Automotive operating system. The standalone app, which is launching today in select Audi models, runs directly on the vehicle’s infotainment hardware — eliminating the need for phone tethering, Bluetooth connections, or aux cables.
Spotify is busting free of CarPlay with the launch of its first native car app
Say goodbye to those aux cables. Spotify’s new in-car app is here, and it’s rolling out to Audi vehicles today.
It’s the clearest sign yet that Spotify is ready to move beyond Apple CarPlay and Android, popular phone projection systems that currently dominate the way most people consume media in their cars. And with 34 percent of Spotify’s monthly active users and 77 percent of Premium subscribers streaming music in their cars, the platform they use to listen has never been more important.
Spotify’s new native app will launch with several Audi models, including the electric A6 e-tron and Q6 e-tron, as well as the gas-powered A5, Q5, and A6. Jonathan Tarlton, Spotify’s automotive business development lead, said the app, which has been in development for a little more than a year, is about delivering a more inviting experience to users — and specifically one that’s completely controlled by Spotify.
Spotify’s standard Android Automotive app operated as a “headless” integration, meaning that Spotify supplied the underlying backend data, playlists, and music catalog, but Google’s templates dictated how the interface was drawn and structured onscreen. The new Audi application is “headful,” allowing Spotify to draw and render its own native UI directly on the vehicle’s screens from scratch.
“We’re drawing all the pixels,” Tarlton said in an interview. “We own the user experience. So we’re not in a template or a framework. It’s 100 percent Spotify.”
To be sure, Spotify isn’t turning its back on Apple CarPlay and Android Auto; the company is still “heavily invested” in phone projection, Tarlton assured us. That said, the native Spotify app is being set up to compete directly with phone mirroring. Apple CarPlay and Android Auto remain the default way many people listen to music or podcasts in their vehicles: Drivers get in, connect their phones automatically, and tap into their familiar mobile interface. A native Spotify app could encourage people to listen through the car’s own operating system instead of projecting their phones — a scenario that Tarlton says he welcomes.
“We’re drawing all the pixels. We own the user experience. So we’re not in a template or a framework. It’s 100 percent Spotify.”
— Jonathan Tarlton, head of automotive business development at Spotify
“We want to give users choice,” he said. “We want to be wherever they are and we want to make sure that they’re accessing Spotify in the way they want to access it, whether they’re locked into the iOS ecosystem … or Android on the phone as well.”
People may love their CarPlay, but the experience is not without its tradeoffs. Wireless connection, in particular, can be spotty depending on your vehicle. Tarlton said the new app is aimed at reducing some of those headaches, like “a cold start in the morning,” he said. “You’re not having to wait to boot. You’re not having to wait for a screen to load. You’re not having to plug your phone in.”
There are other benefits to using the native Spotify app over a projected one from your phone. Passengers can scan a QR code displayed on the screen to join a wireless “Spotify Jam” session and add songs directly to the queue from their smartphones. On vehicles with a dedicated secondary passenger display, front passengers can browse, view lyrics, and watch video content without disturbing the driver. And while the vehicle is parked or charging, those motion graphics, like video podcasts and lyrics, move to the central display so everyone can enjoy.
With these features in particular, Spotify feels like it’s doing its part in helping to bring car passengers together again, Tarlton said. Often today you’ll find parents rocking out to their favorite hits in the front while kids are wearing their headphones in the back. The new app aims to correct that dynamic. “I’m excited that we can bring joy to the cabin again,” he said. “It’s not just technology.”
The rollout of the new Spotify app will focus in particular on cars with Android-based operating systems, he said. In that way, Spotifty can avoid having to build separate, bespoke applications for every individual automaker. Rather, the company can use a standard Android Automotive APK that it can then distribute through multiple app stores, whether it’s the Google Play Store or proprietary automaker stores like the Audi Application Store.
“Our number one goal was to prevent fragmentation, not just for our sake, but for the sake of the whole industry,” Tarlton said, “because we believe in having an open and fair place for apps to play — and the car is such a great place for that.”

title: I can’t get enough of the iPhone Duo’s matte inner display
summary: The iPhone Duo has all the messiness of a first-gen product. And while I’m not sure I love all of the decisions Apple made around its design, it got one thing right: the matte finish on the inner screen. I’ve been using it for the past week to watch movies on a plane, peruse my photo gallery, and ca...
content:
The iPhone Duo has all the messiness of a first-gen product. And while I’m not sure I love all of the decisions Apple made around its design, it got one thing right: the matte finish on the inner screen. I’ve been using it for the past week to watch movies on a plane, peruse my photo gallery, and catch up on a little reading, and I’m convinced. The matte screen is the best thing about the Duo, and I hope every other foldable maker copies it.
I can’t get enough of the iPhone Duo’s matte inner display
Nano-texture was the right move.
Nano-texture was the right move.
When we first got our hands on the Duo, the nano-texture finish on the 7.6-inch inner screen was genuinely a surprise. I’ve used a dozen or so book-style foldables over the past five years, and every one of them came with a glossy inner display. Aside from occasionally noting that they can be hard to see in direct sun, I never really questioned it. That’s just how screens are, I figured. But opening up the Duo for the first time, it clicked. Matte makes sense.
The benefits proved out while I used the phone for the past seven days. I propped it up on my tray table to watch an episode of Widow’s Bay. The matte screen effectively fought off the glare from the open window in my row. Reading a longer article felt a little easier on the eyes, and that’s what the inner screen is really there for. And there’s something about that slight matte finish that signals to my brain that it’s time to read. I can sort of fool myself into thinking that I’m holding an e-reader when I open the Kindle app and turn the phone sideways to its portrait orientation. It’s cute to imagine using your reading app in the landscape-oriented, partway-closed posture like a physical book. But I wouldn’t actually read anything like that; portrait all the way.
The thing to know about the Duo’s matte finish is that it’s pretty subtle. You don’t feel it under your finger quite as much as the more paperlike finish on TCL’s Nxtpaper devices. My colleague Dominic Preston wondered if it would be jarring flipping between the glossy cover screen and the matte display, and personally it hasn’t bothered me. The fact that the Duo’s big screen isn’t full-on e-reader matte probably helps ease that transition.
In fact, changing between the two screens somehow feels nice in both directions. Opening up to the inner screen feels like a welcome break from the reflections on the outer screen. When closing it and going back to the outer screen, the richer blacks and colors feel inviting.
I can concede that if you’re watching something with a lot of dark, shadowy scenes, the matte might feel like it obscures a bit of the detail that would otherwise stand out. It didn’t really bother me. But the bottom line is that this is a device that you will, by its nature, take outside. You’ll use it in ideal lighting conditions and crappy ones. I’ll take a slight hit in richness and detail for a more comfortable overall viewing experience. When my seatmate throws the window shade open, I’ll be ready for it.

title: The iPhone Duo is a messy, expensive, good time
summary: The iPhone Duo is the riskiest Apple product in years. It’s a huge rethink of what an iPhone is and could be, and it contains the seeds of many fascinating ideas that might be great in the future. The iPhone Duo is a messy, expensive, good time Apple’s first foldable is an early adopter special. If ...
content:
The iPhone Duo is the riskiest Apple product in years. It’s a huge rethink of what an iPhone is and could be, and it contains the seeds of many fascinating ideas that might be great in the future.
The iPhone Duo is a messy, expensive, good time
Apple’s first foldable is an early adopter special.
If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.
But that future is yet to come. The iPhone Duo is also one of Apple’s messiest first-generation products in a long time, and right now it will delight gadget nerds and early adopters and likely frustrate everyone else.
It’s been a minute since the iPhone has looked or worked significantly differently. The last major change was the iPhone X, which dropped the home button almost a decade ago, and even that was a fairly subtle improvement. In fact, “subtle improvement” is really the entire story of the iPhone — it’s the foundation of Apple’s entire business, after all, and there’s a lot of risk in just up and changing it. You can see it in this year’s iPhone 18 Pro: It’s been refined in many ways, with better thermals and an interesting variable aperture lens, but it’s barely different than the iPhone 17 Pro.
But you can’t play it safe designing a foldable. You have to make some big decisions about screen sizes and what the inner and outer displays are for, and then make an even bigger set of decisions about how that big inner screen should work. All of those decisions are risky, and Apple’s riskiest decision was the Duo’s size and shape.
iPhone Duo
The Good
- Fun to play with
- Matte inner display is very cool
- You will watch less TikTok on it
The Bad
- You will watch less TikTok on it because the cover display is too small
- Heavier and bulkier than a standard phone
- Gets hot
- Cameras are just OK
Hardware and design
Apple’s single most important design decision for the Duo was to make it shaped like a passport.
The wide aspect ratio makes the inner screen friendlier for 16:9 YouTube videos, but it also marks a departure from the taller foldable design phone makers have embraced over the past five years. Prior to 2026, most folding phones opted for a tall-and-narrow shape to optimize for using vertical apps on the cover screen. But rumors started pointing to Apple going with its landscape-first form factor, and other foldable makers shifted gears — seemingly to get ahead of Apple. Now that the iPhone and a handful of competitors have adopted the wide format, they have to solve a new problem: designing a cover screen that will work well enough for vertically oriented apps.
The Duo’s 5.4-inch outer display is glossy, while the 7.6-inch inner display has a striking nano-texture matte coating. Apple’s very proud of this inner matte display, and for good reason — it looks and feels incredibly solid, a big step up from foldables with glossy, seemingly soft screens with glaringly obvious creases, like the Pixel Fold, and even the more subtle but still visible crease of the Galaxy Fold 8.
The matte display is indeed there to help hide the crease, which Apple keeps calling “perceptually flat” because it’s more fun to invent science-y marketing phrases than just saying “you mostly don’t see it.” But it’s true: You mostly can’t see the display crease, although you can definitely feel it. If you’re looking at a white image off-axis, you can see it, and there are moments in some lighting where it’s much more obvious. It definitely shows up more prominently on camera than it does to your eyes.
What you will see is the under-display camera, which reflects light in a more glossy way if you’re outdoors or in a bright area. Overall, though, the camera and display crease stopped being noticeable after a while. The crease also wasn’t any more noticeable after a week of constant flipping and folding, although we’ll see how it holds up over time.
That’ll be a real test, because Duo owners are going to be constantly flipping this thing open. Between Apple’s display aspect ratio and iOS design choices, the outer screen feels like much more of a status display than you’d expect — everything about the Duo gently nudges you to flip it open and use it in tablet mode. And not just tablet mode, but portrait tablet mode. That’s because iPhone apps are largely portrait, and the Duo is still very much an iPhone, even though its shape makes it fight all that history.
iPhones have gotten bigger over the years, but they’ve mostly stuck to the same basic rectangular aspect ratios: 2:3 from the first iPhone through the 4S, 16:9 from the iPhone 5 through the 8, and 19.5:9 from the iPhone X on to today’s iPhone 18 Pro. Basically, the iPhone has mostly gotten taller over time.
It’s wild to have iPhone apps with controls in all kinds of different places
The Duo changes all of that — it’s the first iPhone that’s gotten shorter and wider. Both the inner and outer displays have a 1.4:1 aspect ratio, which was a very deliberate choice on Apple’s part, because they’re the same shape open and closed. This is clever in terms of display math and potentially great for app developers, but in practice it means that the outer display is really quite small, especially compared to modern Max-sized phones. If you’re texting someone in Messages with the keyboard onscreen, you’re lucky to be able to see two or three texts at once.
Apple has tried to reclaim some vertical space by scooting the UI elements of updated apps off to the right, but if you’re left-handed, that means using the phone closed with one hand can be challenging, even for someone with big hands. Having that strip of real estate along the right side occupied by navigation controls also means that using the Duo single-handed in your right forces you to reach farther when there’s something on the left side of the screen you need to tap. This means that you’re sometimes holding a fairly heavy phone, stretching for a small target that’s just out of reach, which isn’t particularly confidence-inspirin

title: Astronauts’ hearts just passed a surprising test for Mars
summary: Astronauts’ hearts just passed a surprising test for Mars - Date: - October 21, 2026 - Source: - Northwestern University - Summary: - A new study tracking 13 astronauts suggests that the human heart may be surprisingly well equipped for a journey to Mars, especially with regular exercise during spac...
content:
Astronauts’ hearts just passed a surprising test for Mars
- Date:
- October 21, 2026
- Source:
- Northwestern University
- Summary:
- A new study tracking 13 astronauts suggests that the human heart may be surprisingly well equipped for a journey to Mars, especially with regular exercise during spaceflight. Researchers found that astronauts' hearts adapted to months of weightlessness and handled simulated Martian gravity without major problems, offering new hope for future missions to the Red Planet.
- Share:
A journey to Mars may be less challenging for the human heart than scientists once feared. A new study suggests that astronauts can adapt remarkably well to months of weightlessness, offering encouraging evidence that humans could endure the long trip to the Red Planet and function under its weaker gravity.
Researchers from Northwestern Medicine, UT Southwestern, and UT Houston monitored the hearts of 13 astronauts who spent approximately six months aboard the International Space Station. Their findings showed that although spaceflight initially affected heart performance, the astronauts gradually adapted, with intensive daily exercise playing an important role in maintaining their cardiovascular health.
One of NASA's major concerns about sending humans to Mars is how astronauts' hearts and circulatory systems will respond when they leave the weightless conditions of spaceflight (known as microgravity) and encounter Martian gravity, which is only about one-third as strong as Earth's.
Encouragingly, the researchers found that the astronauts showed no significant signs of cardiovascular strain when exposed to simulated Martian gravity after returning to Earth.
"With our findings, there is now reason to think that we would be able to traverse to Mars, get there and actually work on the surface of Mars," said study senior author Dr. James Thomas, professor of medicine in the division of cardiology at Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine.
The study, published last month in the journal Circulation, is the first to investigate how the heart responds to simulated Martian gravity following an extended period in space.
How Daily Exercise Protects Astronauts' Hearts in Space
Living without gravity creates unusual challenges for the human body. On Earth, the heart constantly works against gravity to circulate blood, while muscles must support the body's weight. In space, those demands decrease substantially, allowing muscles and even the heart itself to shrink over time.
Returning to a gravitational environment can also be difficult. Astronauts on previous missions have frequently experienced dizziness or lightheadedness when standing after landing. This happens because gravity pulls blood toward the lower body, sometimes causing blood pressure to drop suddenly. The condition is called orthostatic hypotension. (If you've seen Sandra Bullock crawling after returning to Earth in "Gravity," you get the idea.)
However, the astronauts involved in the new study generally handled this transition well, potentially because they had maintained demanding exercise schedules throughout their missions.
As part of NASA's Exercise Countermeasures program, astronauts exercised for up to two hours each day. Their routines included 30 to 45 minutes of endurance training, which strengthens the cardiovascular system, along with 60 to 75 minutes of resistance training to help preserve muscle mass and strength.
"You lose muscle mass and cardiac mass when you're in a weightless environment because you are working less up there," explained Thomas, who also is a Northwestern Medicine cardiologist. "You're floating around in the air, and you give a little tap with your foot, and you can sail over to say hello to your buddy."
"To counter that, exercise is crucial when you're in space," Thomas added.
Heart Scans Reveal How the Body Adapts to Weightlessness
To understand what happens to the heart during prolonged spaceflight, the researchers collected echocardiograms before, during, and after each astronaut's mission. These ultrasound scans use sound waves to produce moving images of the heart, allowing doctors to examine its structure and measure how effectively it pumps blood.
While aboard the International Space Station, astronauts were trained to perform these scans on one another every few weeks. The recordings were transmitted to Earth, where researchers could monitor changes in heart function throughout the missions.
Thomas worked alongside Dr. Benjamin Levine of UT Southwestern Medical Center and Dr. Michael Bungo of the McGovern Medical School at UTHealth Houston.
"It would be typically about 3 a.m. for me because the space station runs on Greenwich Mean Time," Thomas said. "I would watch the recordings come in live and coach the astronauts in real time to improve the images."
The scans revealed that the astronauts' hearts initially struggled to adjust to their new environment. During the first two weeks in space, researchers observed declines in cardiac filling, stroke volume, and several other measures of cardiovascular performance.
Cardiac filling refers to how much blood enters the heart between beats, while stroke volume describes the amount of blood pumped out with each contraction. Both measurements decreased early in the missions, indicating that the astronauts' hearts were temporarily moving less blood with each beat.
But the changes did not persist.
As the astronauts spent more time in space, their cardiovascular systems adapted. Cardiac filling and stroke volume gradually improved, approaching the levels recorded before launch.
These results suggest that the heart can adjust to prolonged weightlessness more effectively than early measurements might indicate, particularly when astronauts maintain regular physical activity.

title: Up to 20% of MS diagnoses may be wrong, like Christina Applegate's
summary: Up to 20% of MS diagnoses are wrong, like Christina Applegate's. Here's what doctors say patients should know. Actor Christina Applegate announced Tuesday that she had been misdiagnosed with multiple sclerosis after years of believing she had the condition — and experts say her experience is more co...
content:
Up to 20% of MS diagnoses are wrong, like Christina Applegate's. Here's what doctors say patients should know.
Actor Christina Applegate announced Tuesday that she had been misdiagnosed with multiple sclerosis after years of believing she had the condition — and experts say her experience is more common than many people realize.
Applegate shared the news on her podcast, MeSsy, where she and actor Jamie-Lynn Sigler discuss life with MS. In a follow-up episode, Dr. Marwa Kaisey, an associate professor at the Cedars-Sinai Medical Center department of neurology, said that almost 1 in 5 people who are told they have multiple sclerosis "didn't actually have it."
There is no single test to confirm MS, a disease where the body's immune system attacks the central nervous system. Symptoms vary from person to person and it can progress in different ways, according to the National Multiple Sclerosis Society.
How can an MS misdiagnosis be discovered?
CBS News spoke with Dr. Robert Bermel, the director of the Mellen Center for MS at Cleveland Clinic, a multidisciplinary center that cares for more than 11,000 patients with multiple sclerosis, about the risk of an MS misdiagnosis and what patients need to know.
He said a misdiagnosis is most often found when a person seeks out a second opinion because their symptoms aren't getting better. This doesn't always mean the diagnosis is wrong, but can be an indicator for more advanced tests. (Bermel said most MS treatments, especially the ones most commonly used, are "very safe" and wouldn't put a person's health in danger.)
When a misdiagnosis happens, the root cause is typically that abnormalities on brain scans were misinterpreted, Bermel said. Lesions on the brain are considered a hallmark of MS, but they can also be caused by other medical issues such as high blood pressure, smoking or migraines. More advanced MRI sequences can help differentiate between MS lesions and those caused by other conditions, Bermel said.
When concerns about a potential misdiagnosis arise, the next steps typically involve running specialized tests. Those can include advanced MRI sequences to study the lesions more closely, a spinal MRI, or spinal fluid analysis that can identify specific abnormal immune proteins, Bermel said.
How common is an MS misdiagnosis?
On MeSsy, Kaisey described MS misdiagnoses as "fairly common." Bermel said that the largest studies looking at the risk of misdiagnosis have shown that between 15% and 20% of patients diagnosed with MS are found to not actually have the condition.
Dr. Josef Gutman, the director of NYU Langone's Long Island Comprehensive MS Care Center, told CBS News that the wide spectrum of symptoms that can be attributed to multiple sclerosis makes the condition difficult to diagnosis.
"It's important to keep in mind that those symptoms are not necessarily specific in a lot of ways. It's sort of the story, combined with MRI imaging, combined with other markers like spinal fluid, that help us make the MS diagnosis," Gutman said. "It's not like diabetes, where there's one blood test and if it's above this number, it's diabetes, if it's below this number, it isn't. There's a lot of things going into the diagnosis."
New multiple sclerosis diagnostic criteria, developed by an international panel of experts in the field, were published in 2025 to try to reduce this risk. These criteria are more specific than before, according to Bermel, especially when it comes to interpreting brain lesions.
"We really place a high premium on getting the diagnosis correct from the start, so that then we can move very confidently into highly effective therapy for MS," Bermel said.
What happens after an MS misdiagnosis?
If a patient's multiple sclerosis misdiagnosis is identified, doctors will then start looking at other potential causes for their symptoms, Bermel said.
They may be suffering from an autoimmune condition, which can cause joint pain, swelling and system-wide inflammation. Fibromyalgia is a "commonly identified diagnosis that mimics MS," Bermel said. Migraines are also a possible diagnosis, because migraine can cause lesions and other neurological symptoms. Chronic pain or fatigue syndromes can also "masquerade as MS," Bermel said.
Sometimes, a person may not have one disorder but several, Bermel said, noting that an incorrect diagnosis "really sidetracks things."
"MS can sometimes be a gratifying solution to a patient with many symptoms because it's thought of as kind of a single, solitary root cause of things," he said, adding that he has seen patients whose fatigue is caused by a sleep or thyroid disorder, while rheumatoid conditions or fibromyalgia cause pain and swelling.
On her podcast, Applegate said learning she had the wrong diagnosis has made things harder for now, since there's still no explanation for the debilitating symptoms that affect her daily life and mobility.
"You don't get misdiagnosed and then all of the sudden I'm better," Applegate said. "If anything, I've gotten worse. So I'm back at square one where I don't know what's going on with me. And that's going to be an online investigation that my doctors are going to be getting into just to find out what has been going on since 2021, why did this happen?"
When to seek out a second opinion
While only a minority of patients are misdiagnosed, anyone concerned about their diagnosis should always feel comfortable seeking a second opinion, Bermel said. Even when the original diagnosis is correct, a second opinion can help a patient find other resources, he noted.
"MS is a life-changing diagnosis, and anytime somebody is facing something like that, I always think a second opinion is potentially in order," Bermel said.
Patients can also seek out a multiple sclerosis expert, Bermel said. The National Multiple Sclerosis Society maintains an online registry and map of care centers and MS specialists nationwide. Bermel called that list a "really good starting point to identify" nearby resour

title: A critical PHP vulnerability may take websites down today
summary: Security patches for the PHP programming language, widely used to build websites and web apps, are expected to roll out today, with the goal of fixing two critical vulnerabilities that could wreak havoc on the internet if left unchecked. In an advisory published on Tuesday, PHP developers said the v...
content:
Security patches for the PHP programming language, widely used to build websites and web apps, are expected to roll out today, with the goal of fixing two critical vulnerabilities that could wreak havoc on the internet if left unchecked. In an advisory published on Tuesday, PHP developers said the vulnerabilities have a severity rating of 9.2 out of a possible 10, with some cybersecurity agencies encouraging websites to temporarily take their systems offline if they’re unable to apply the fix immediately.
A critical PHP vulnerability may take websites down today
A patch is about to roll out, but the exploit affects more than 40 percent of the internet.
The security patch is expected to drop today at 10AM ET — though the developers say they may release it earlier if the vulnerability details become public or there’s evidence of the exploits actively being used — and PHP users are being urged to “upgrade as soon as the release is available.” According to cybersecurity firm watchTowr, the vulnerabilities are Remote Code Execution exploits that reportedly impact every PHP version from PHP 5 onward, and could enable attackers to run their own code on affected servers, allowing them to maliciously alter websites, steal data, and more.
The impact of these vulnerabilities could be vast, with one security researcher estimating that more than 1.3 million internet-connected hosts are likely affected. WordPress security plugin provider Wordfence also warned that every WordPress site will be vulnerable because they all run on servers that use PHP, which is no small number given WordPress reported last year that it powers more than 40 percent of the internet. Wordfence also warned that the fix can’t be installed using automatic updates, so site owners need to find out who is responsible for updating PHP to apply the patch manually.
The European Union Computer Emergency Response Team and the UK National Cyber Security Centre have both issued advisories that encourage any companies who can’t immediately patch their platforms to instead isolate their internet-facing apps from public networks or take them offline entirely until the vulnerabilities can be fully mitigated. Mobile operating system developer GrapheneOS says they’ve temporarily taken their user discussion forum offline because proof of concept exploits are already being developed and they “don’t want to take the risk.” According to PHP developer Gina Peter Banyard, patching is the only mitigation, and otherwise turning servers off “might be the most sensible thing to do.”
Multiple cybersecurity organizations have also prompted PHP admins to prepare, with threat researchers at Sansec saying they expect to see “mass attacks within 15 minutes of the release.” That doesn’t mean attackers are waiting around, however. Cloudflare chief technology officer Dane Knecht says “we are seeing early attacks emerging” against the platform’s PHP sites, and that Cloudflare is temporarily updating its firewall rules as a stopgap until the fix is available.

content:
DOJ's noncitizen voter list is unreliable, officials say. And, U.S. pollution rises
Zelenskyy Mending Ties, Trump In North Carolina, Saudi Arabia Gets British Support
Good morning. You're reading the Up First newsletter. Subscribe here to get it delivered to your inbox, and listen to the Up First podcast for all the news you need to start your day.
Today's top stories
Los Angeles County election officials say that the Justice Department's list of 20,000 "likely" noncitizens registered to vote is "unreliable," based on their preliminary analysis. They also say some of the individuals on the list have indicated they were born in the U.S. and may be citizens. State and local officials disclosed these new details in court filings yesterday, in response to a federal lawsuit demanding that California investigate thousands of voters before their ballots are counted. The DOJ wants the state to segregate ballots associated with these individuals. California officials say the DOJ's request is unfeasible so close to the election and may violate federal and state election laws.
A new report from United Nations scientists says that countries are not doing enough to cut emissions that drive climate change, and the United States plays a significant role in climate pollution. The U.S. was the only major economy that saw an increase last year in planet-warming pollution. The report also found that, among G20 countries, the U.S. is tied with Russia for the highest per capita emissions. While China emits more total greenhouse gases annually than the U.S., China's population is more than four times that of the U.S. The rise in U.S. emissions was fueled by increased electricity demand and Trump administration policies that support burning fossil fuels.
Arrests for low-level crimes, including vagrancy and drug possession, increased in the U.S. from 2024 to 2025, according to a new analysis of federal data from the criminal justice and immigration reforms advocacy group FWD.us. The report also highlighted a 188% increase in immigration violations. This comes as violent crime rates, including homicides, dropped to historic lows. The report examined publicly available FBI and immigration arrest data and does not include details about whether charges were dropped or if people served any time in jail or prison. This data covers the first full year of Trump's second term, during which his administration emphasized a tough-on-crime approach. Zoë Towns, the executive director of FWD.us, told NPR ahead of the report's release that the rising trends signal a "really troubling return to some of the extreme law and order policies that defined the American criminal justice system during the '80s and '90s." Check out NPR's analysis.
President Trump's envoy Steve Witkoff is in St. Petersburg today to meet with Kremlin officials and explore potential solutions for ending Russia's war on Ukraine. Witkoff also met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy this week in Norway. Trump has accused Zelenskyy of obstructing a peace deal. The Ukrainian president says he is again seeking direct talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
- 🎧 Norway and Finland's leaders believe a fair deal to end the war requires U.S. involvement, NPR's Joanna Kakissis tells Up First. They hope Witkoff's Russia leads to something constructive. But Ukrainians whom Kakissis has spoken to say they don't trust the White House and believe the U.S. is siding with Russia. Concerns grew among Ukrainians when President Trump announced he would lift sanctions on Russian diesel. Many argued that the move wouldn't lower fuel prices but instead help Russia continue its war against Ukraine.
On the ground
The results of the 2026 midterm elections will shape the final two years of President Trump's second term and serve as a precursor to the 2028 general election. This month, Morning Edition is reporting from six states that could change the balance of power in Washington.
This week, Morning Edition's Steve Inskeep traveled to North Carolina and Georgia. Both states are among those Trump visited this week as he continues to campaign for Republicans vying to keep control of the Senate and House. Inskeep explored how the Trump administration's policies have affected public research in both states. Trump has eliminated hundreds of jobs from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, which is headquartered in Atlanta. Universities and research firms in North Carolina's Research Triangle lost millions of dollars in federal grants last year. Inskeep spoke with people affected by these changes. Listen to what they had to say.
Hear more from voters in both states:
- 🎧 Inskeep got personal thoughts from random Georgia voters by knocking on some doors and meeting people along walking trails.
- 🎧 In North Carolina, he visited communities devastated by Hurricane Helene in 2024 to assess changes two years after the federal response became a campaign issue.
- 🎧 In Stokes County, N.C., Inskeep explores how AI data centers have divided the community. In 2024, 79% of voters in the county backed Trump. The president has supported these centers.

Follow the reporting: Ohio and Michigan coverage airs Oct. 27. You can follow along on Morning Edition, NPR.org, in the NPR app and in this newsletter.

title: Overton would consider Ashes return if Root asks
summary: Overton would consider Ashes return if Root asks - Published England all-rounder Jamie Overton would consider returning to play Test cricket for next year's Ashes if approached by captain Joe Root. Overton played in England's final Test of the home summer in 2025 against India and was in line for a ...
content:
Overton would consider Ashes return if Root asks
- Published
England all-rounder Jamie Overton would consider returning to play Test cricket for next year's Ashes if approached by captain Joe Root.
Overton played in England's final Test of the home summer in 2025 against India and was in line for a place on last winter's Ashes tour, only to take what he described as an "indefinite break" from red-ball cricket.
The 32-year-old, who has a history of stress fractures in his back, has focused on limited-overs cricket since and is part of the England squad for the ongoing one-day tri-series in Pakistan.
Speaking to BBC Sport, Overton said England white-ball captain Harry Brook has asked about the possibility of the Surrey man making himself available for Test cricket.
"To be honest, I haven't thought about it," said Overton. "Brooky's mentioned it to me a couple of times, but I've literally not thought about it."
On the prospect of Root reaching out about the Ashes, Overton added: "If Rooty comes to me and says that then, yeah, then I'll have to have a serious think about it.
"I've always said it was an indefinite break. People think I've retired or whatever, but, no, it was a break that I could focus on my white-ball cricket and being really good in my white-ball cricket."
Overton's appearance in the fifth Test against India in July of 2025 was his second Test cap, three years after his first.
The pace bowler had played only four first-class matches in the two years leading up to his return to the Test team.
When England lost Chris Woakes to a dislocated shoulder, Overton was left as one of three frontline seamers in the XI and sent down 38 overs in the match.
A month later, he announced his hiatus from red-ball cricket, ruling himself out of the Ashes tour in the process.
- Sloppy England start winter with Pakistan defeat 
  - Published20 hours ago
- England coach should be English, suggests Fleming 
  - Published1 day ago
"I came off that Test match against India and I felt physically broken," he said. "I know we lost the bowler, Wokesey went down with a shoulder injury, but that's the worst I felt in playing cricket for a long time.
"It nearly took me two weeks to get ready to play in The Hundred, when you only bowl 20 balls. My shoulder was incredibly sore for two weeks and it just felt like it was an injury waiting to happen if I kept trying to push myself.
"At that point I was just like: 'Let's focus on my white-ball and red-ball cricket might come back'. I've never said I've ruled it out completely."
In the aftermath of Ben Stokes' retirement, England have opted to field four frontline seamers in their XI, with Dan Lawrence batting at number six and offering some off-spin.
If England needed to alter the balance of their side, a returning Overton would be an option to strengthen their lower-order batting. He made 99 on his Test debut against New Zealand in 2022.
"I've never said I've ruled it out," said Overton. "It's just got to be the right thing at the right time.
"It's been just over a year and I've been really structured with my workloads and my plans and getting my body into a good spot. I feel really good."
Jamie's twin brother Craig has played in eight Tests, including in the Ashes series of 2017-18 and 2019.
Craig had a superb summer for Somerset, though told BBC Sport earlier this month he had not been contacted by England about the possibility of a recall.
For Jamie, after turning down the chance of a trip down under last year, Australia's visit to the UK next summer is likely to represent the last chance for a taste of Ashes cricket.
"At that moment I didn't feel like it was the right thing for my body," he said.
"The opportunity to play in the Ashes is every kid's dream. I watched Craig do it and was incredibly proud of what he did. Obviously, you want to be there and do it one day."
Overton was part of the England team beaten by Pakistan in their tri-series opener in Rawalpindi on Tuesday.
England meet Sri Lanka at the same ground on Thursday, with full commentary of that match on Test Match Special via BBC Sounds, BBC Radio 5 live sports extra and the BBC Sport website and app.

title: Un Pemex cada vez más chico
summary: Las cosas en Pemex están que arden. La estrategia para recortar personal de confianza y adelgazar la estructura ya comenzó a sentirse en filiales estratégicas y en niveles altos de la petrolera. De acuerdo con fuentes cercanas, la administración Juan Carlos Carpio no solamente está despidiendo a per...
content:
Las cosas en Pemex están que arden. La estrategia para recortar personal de confianza y adelgazar la estructura ya comenzó a sentirse en filiales estratégicas y en niveles altos de la petrolera.
De acuerdo con fuentes cercanas, la administración Juan Carlos Carpio no solamente está despidiendo a personal de confianza con alto nivel de especialización técnica y financiera, sino que está obligando a otros a aceptar plazas de menor nivel salarial con la misma carga de responsabilidades, o incluso más.
Documentos entregados a este espacio dan cuenta de los movimientos de plazas, con bajas de entre dos hasta siete niveles dentro del escalafón de Pemex, con la promesa de respetar la antigüedad dentro de la empresa estatal.
Los firmantes no tienen opción, “copelan o cuello”. Pemex tiene la sartén por el mango. Una cosa es recortar empleos, como lo hacen todas las empresas del mundo, pero otra muy diferente es degradar a quienes sacan la chamba. No hay razón que valga.
Recordemos que como parte del Plan Estratégico de Pemex 2025-2035, el Consejo de Administración aprobó la cancelación de 3 mil 51 puestos de confianza, equivalentes al 14 por ciento del total de su plantilla laboral, con la finalidad de ahorrar más de 4 mil millones de pesos anuales.
A partir de ahí, la petrolera ha aplicado recortes periódicos, que por cierto, no se han traducido en mejoras ni operativas, ni mucho menos financieras, como se prometió en repetidas ocasiones, e incluso, desde la conferencia mañanera de la presidente Claudia Sheinbaum.
La estrategia de Pemex es dura, considerando los lamentables resultados operativos en la mayor parte de las actividades de la petrolera. Y una estrategia que por cierto, no toca al sindicato, con quien en septiembre pasado pactó un histórico aumento salarial de 7.5 por ciento. Ojalá la producción de crudo, la ganancias por refinación, y en general la productividad de la compañía, se elevaran en esa misma proporción.
Ni las transferencias y apoyos financieros gubernamentales —que este año serán de casi 271 mil millones de pesos— han podido mejorar la situación en la petrolera nacional.
En el primer semestre de este año Pemex reportó pérdidas por casi 2 mil 350 millones de dólares. La producción de crudo lleva más de dos años estancada en 1.6 millones de barriles diarios. Las refinerías operan a menos de la mitad de su capacidad. Por mencionar algunos tristes indicadores.
Tenemos un Pemex cada vez más chico en un país que promete ser más grande, que tiene un ambicioso Plan México, que defiende la soberanía energética… algo no cuadra.

title: F1 races to return to standard distance in 2028
summary: F1 races to return to standard distance in 2028 - Published Formula 1 grands prix will return to their standard distance in 2028 after the maximum length was shortened for next season. The maximum distance of a race was cut by 15km from 305km (189.5 miles) to 290km (180.2 miles) for the 2027 season....
content:
F1 races to return to standard distance in 2028
- Published
Formula 1 grands prix will return to their standard distance in 2028 after the maximum length was shortened for next season.
The maximum distance of a race was cut by 15km from 305km (189.5 miles) to 290km (180.2 miles) for the 2027 season.
That reduction was introduced because of a quirk of the situation surrounding changes to the engine rules for next year.
The new hybrid engines introduced this year, which have a near 50-50 split between internal combustion and electrical power, have been criticised for reducing the impact of driver skill.
The power split will be changed, in two steps, to 60-40 by 2028, enabling drivers to have maximum power for longer.
This means the cars will use more fuel - and that became a concern when it emerged some teams wanted to carry their chassis over into next year to save money.
As the fuel tank is within the chassis and therefore its size could not be changed, this meant those teams might not have been able to finish grands prix with their existing fuel tanks.
The change affects only a handful of races where fuel consumption is heaviest.
The sport's governing body, the FIA, published the 2027 rules this week and these included a section on changes for 2028 in which there is a clause that removes the reduction and reinstates the 305km maximum distance.
Ferrari driver Lewis Hamilton had previously objected to the shortening of race distances.
Britain's Hamilton, 41, said: "The races should be longer because the races are physically easier than ever before. So shortening, I don't think, makes much sense.
"This is supposed to be the sport that's the most physically demanding - mentally and physically. There are some that are just so hot and ultimately you are on the edge. Like Singapore is incredibly hot and demanding.
"But that's where I think you want to see athletes - just right on the edge, right? Right at the edge of their performance, having to actually push their bodies further because that's what this sport is about - pushing, pushing the levels and pushing the boundaries."

title: The night watch: the YouTubers who were guardians of a shark stuck in a South Korean canal
summary: In South Korea, they call them jagyeongdan, a word whose meaning sits somewhere between vigilante group and neighbourhood watch. Each night they put on hi-vis vests, picked up their selfie sticks and gathered around the harbour in Busan to keep watch over an unlikely charge: a stranded shark affecti...
content:
In South Korea, they call them jagyeongdan, a word whose meaning sits somewhere between vigilante group and neighbourhood watch. Each night they put on hi-vis vests, picked up their selfie sticks and gathered around the harbour in Busan to keep watch over an unlikely charge: a stranded shark affectionately known as Bukang-i.
On Wednesday, after more than a month in the canal and at the third attempt, the shark was successfully guided out, South Korea’s oceans ministry said. Officials expect her to move into open water in time.
For the month that she was stranded, the group of self-appointed guardians took turns to protect her, patrolling the waterfront at night for visitors who might disturb the animal.
Most are YouTubers who livestreamed the waterway, where the shark became a national celebrity. They stayed up through the night, calling out anyone shining torches or lasers into the water. Some of their videos have been watched hundreds of thousands of times.
“They bring fishing lamps, or the kind of lights people use at a campsite,” said Choi Won-jin, one of the shark’s protectors. He would arrive as the lights went out along the canal and wait for the offenders Koreans online call “lantern villains”.
The shark had been marooned in the canal since 18 September. Named after Bukhang, the Korean name for the city’s North Port, and about 3 metres long, the female dusky shark was one of a species classed as endangered worldwide. More than 1.6 million visitors came to see her, the city said, at a park that used to draw about 2,000 people on a busy Saturday.
Authorities had twice tried to guide her back out to sea and failed. Until she left, the shark remained in the canal, drawing crowds by day and leaving a handful of men to keep watch after dark. They patrolled the canal’s park to check everything was in order, ate snacks as the night went by, and shared their grievances on air about the behaviour they witnessed.
“We’re ordinary members of the public,” said Choi, who has had a YouTube channel for 10 years and covers trending issues in South Korea. “So we have no choice but to put it nicely, and get them to understand as best we can.”
“Don’t, please don’t switch the torch on,” said one of them, a YouTuber who lived nearby and went by the name Na Tae-soo. Most people complied, he said. “The animal thrashes about at night because of the torches, and it’s dangerous.”
His footage captured the shark twisting sharply away from a beam of light at 2am and striking the side of the canal. The national institute of fisheries science later confirmed an abrasion on her snout and said a visitor’s torch was likely to have startled the shark into injury.
Korean media reported that 105 officials from seven agencies watched over her, with a team on standby to reach the water within three minutes. Choi disputed this, saying that after dark it was almost up to him and the others.
The waterfront was closed to the public from midnight until 5am, a restriction the YouTubers said was impossible to enforce across a park that size. One night, livestreaming from the walkway, Choi filmed a man tipping food waste into the water.
Nobody saw the shark feed, though experts said feeding could happen in an instant and sharks her size did not need to eat often.
Further attempts to free the shark had been paused on the grounds that more force would distress her.
Cooler water had been expected to prompt her to move on. Dusky sharks prefer water between 18C and 26C, the fisheries institute said. Experts put 15C as the point below which her physiological functions would start to decline, and about 11C as the point at which survival would become precarious. Busan city officials had expected the canal to reach that temperature after the middle of November.
The fisheries institute recorded 46 large sharks off the east coast in the first half of this year, nearly four times as many as a year earlier, which it attributed to warmer seas and more of the fish that sharks feed on.
The affection for Bukang-i has meanwhile become an industry, with a commemorative soju, a baseball mascot in a shark cape and an honorary city ambassadorship, and nearby shops reporting a surge in sales. South Korea’s president, Lee Jae Myung, visited the canal in mid-October.
None of the shark’s guardians thought she should be forced out. Choi said the city should protect her where she was until she left of her own accord.
Kim Jong-hwan, who runs a small business, kept watch by day as well and livestreamed her almost every day. “I went to pass on information [to my followers], and after that I started observing her”, he said. “Watching her over time, with the water pumps being fired and then the nets, I came to find those things being done to her objectionable. So we ended up cheering her on.”
“She’s just an animal, and she came in by her own choice,” Kim said. “If it gets cold, if there’s no food, if the water doesn’t suit her, she’ll leave by herself. I’d like her to just be left alone, to rest there comfortably until then, and go.”

title: El dipuhooligan hace de las suyas, ahora contra Máynez
summary: El diputado Carlos Gutiérrez Mancilla, del PRI, hizo otra vez honor a su apodo de dipuhooligan y ayer se lanzó contra el dirigente de MC, Jorge Álvarez Máynez, en San Lázaro. Le gritó: “¡No seas cobarde, cabrón, da la cara!”, y lo llamó asesino, por “los niños que están muriendo por las infecciones”...
content:
El diputado Carlos Gutiérrez Mancilla, del PRI, hizo otra vez honor a su apodo de dipuhooligan y ayer se lanzó contra el dirigente de MC, Jorge Álvarez Máynez, en San Lázaro. Le gritó: “¡No seas cobarde, cabrón, da la cara!”, y lo llamó asesino, por “los niños que están muriendo por las infecciones” derivadas del agua sucia en Guadalajara, gobernada por Movimiento Ciudadano. El priista fue contenido por emecistas, pues amenazó con golpear a su líder, luego de que intentó y no pudo rociar su rostro con agua hedionda. Eso sí, arrojó el agua puerca a las oficinas de la bancada naranja. Más tarde, Máynez, en un video, lo acusó de realizar “montajes que terminan siendo una burla y una ofensa a la gente” con actitudes de porros.
Cerrojazo guinda a los pataleos de las corcholatas
El proceso ya se cerró. Que ni reclamen en Nuevo León con Tatiana Clouthier, en Zacatecas con José Narro, en Michoacán con Raúl Morón o en Guerrero con Félix Salgado. Las “coordinaciones” estatales “ya están dadas”, aclaró la mandamás en Morena, Ariadna Montiel. Cuestionada principalmente por el berrinche de la Tía Tatis, la dirigente guinda insistió: “Hay un proceso establecido, con normas claras, y cada uno de los aspirantes firmó un compromiso de sujetarse a las reglas”. Y recalcó: “Los políticos tenemos muchas cosas que cuentan, pero fundamentalmente nuestra palabra para con el pueblo, cumplir los compromisos”. Claro… el “pueblo bueno y sabio”.
¿Dónde está el community manager?
Alguien ayúdele con su Facebook a César Jáuregui, exfiscal de Chihuahua, pues aún mantiene en su foto de perfil el eslogan que inventó el panismo en defensa de la gobernadora Maru Campos: “Yo con Maru”. El problema es que Maru ya no está con él, ¡oups!
Senadores morenos, mal y de malas
Quien siguió en la muina fue la senadora Martha Lucía Micher, pues rechazó hablar con la prensa sobre su capricho con las salas VIP de Aeroméxico. Eso sí, se le notó muy corajuda platicando con Javier Corral al concluir la sesión de ayer y hasta dando de manotazos. El chihuahuense, otro que no quiso hablar por el tema de César Jáuregui, incluso la arropó para abandonar el pleno y no dar chance a la insistencia de los reporteros.
Olga, sola en su propia bancada
Otra vez, la bancada de Morena en San Lázaro dejó sola a la ministra en retiro, Olga Sánchez Cordero. La mayoría de la ‘4T’ se impuso y aplazó hasta el 2031 la entrada en vigor del nuevo Código Nacional de Procedimientos Civiles y Familiares, aprobado en la Constitución desde 2017 y creado hasta 2023, pero que sigue sin operar. La exsecretaria de Gobernación y hoy diputada guinda se quejó contra su propia fracción parlamentaria: “Hasta 2031 se prolongaría este vacío procesal y podría comprometer la protección del patrimonio, el acceso a la justicia y el ejercicio de otros derechos fundamentales de las personas con discapacidad y de las personas mayores”. Pero nadie la escuchó.
El amor del pueblo
Con la novedad de que la presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum hizo un recorrido por el Hospital Oncológico La Pastora, del IMSS Bienestar, en la alcaldía Gustavo A. Madero. Pese a la situación del sector, la morenista se encontró con puros simpatizantes que se abalanzaron sobre su vehículo para saludarla y tomarse una selfie. “Claudia, no estás sola, llegamos todas” y “Claudia, escucha, la GAM está en tu lucha”, le gritaron. Aquello, más que un recorrido por un hospital, parecía más bien un mitin de apoyo. Son los tiempos.

title: Cómo activar el modo IA de Google Maps y qué funciones tiene
summary: Cómo activar el modo IA de Google Maps y qué funciones tiene La aplicación incorporó nuevas herramientas de inteligencia artificial que permiten buscar lugares, modificar recorridos y consultar información mediante comandos de voz - 3 minutos de lectura' Google Maps se convirtió en una de las aplica...
content:
Cómo activar el modo IA de Google Maps y qué funciones tiene
La aplicación incorporó nuevas herramientas de inteligencia artificial que permiten buscar lugares, modificar recorridos y consultar información mediante comandos de voz
- 3 minutos de lectura'
Google Maps se convirtió en una de las aplicaciones más utilizadas para encontrar direcciones, consultar el estado del tránsito y descubrir nuevos lugares para conocer, incluso estando a miles de kilómetros de distancia. Sin embargo, la incorporación de Gemini, la inteligencia artificial de Google, transformó la manera en que los usuarios interactúan con esta herramienta, al permitir realizar consultas y recibir indicaciones sin necesidad de escribir.
Esta integración ofrece al usuario la posibilidad de conversar con la IA y solicitarle cambios en los trayectos, buscar establecimientos y obtener información relacionada con la ubicación a la que quieren acceder con instrucciones de un lenguaje más coloquial. De esta forma, la aplicación deja de limitarse a mostrar recorridos y suma funciones similares a las de un asistente virtual.
Por el momento, las nuevas funciones de inteligencia artificial se incorporan de manera gradual, por lo que su disponibilidad puede variar según el dispositivo, la región y la versión de Google Maps instalada.
Es por eso que, para utilizar las funciones de Gemini dentro de Google Maps en dispositivos Android e iPhone, es importante contar con las aplicaciones actualizadas y comprobar que la integración esté habilitada. Los pasos para acceder a esta herramienta son los siguientes:
- Actualizar Google Maps: ingresar a Google Play Store, buscar la aplicación y comprobar si existe una actualización pendiente.
- Configurar Gemini: abrir la aplicación de Gemini y, si el dispositivo lo permite, seleccionarlo como asistente digital predeterminado.
- Revisar los permisos: comprobar que Google Maps tenga acceso a la ubicación y habilitar los permisos adicionales que requieran las funciones de Gemini que se deseen utilizar.
- Iniciar un recorrido: abrir Google Maps, seleccionar un destino y comenzar la navegación.
- Activar el asistente de voz: presionar el ícono del micrófono ubicado en la pantalla de navegación. En los dispositivos compatibles, este acceso permite interactuar con Gemini.
- Realizar una consulta: pedir indicaciones, buscar establecimientos cercanos o solicitar modificaciones en el recorrido mediante comandos de voz.
Una de las señales que permiten identificar la integración es la aparición del símbolo característico de Gemini, representado por un destello, cuando se activa el asistente.
¿Cuáles son los prompts más útiles para utilizar en la IA de Google Maps?
Entre los prompts más útiles para aprovechar la inteligencia artificial de Google Maps se encuentran:
- Para encontrar restaurantes: “Buscá un restaurante cerca de mi ubicación que tenga buenas reseñas y precios accesibles”.
- Para evitar demoras: “Mostrame una ruta alternativa para llegar a mi destino y evitar el tránsito”.
- Para organizar paradas: “Buscá una estación de servicio que quede de camino a mi destino”.
- Para descubrir lugares turísticos: “Recomendame cinco lugares interesantes para visitar cerca de donde estoy”.
- Para evitar peajes: “Mostrame cómo llegar a mi destino sin pasar por rutas con peajes”.
- Para buscar comercios abiertos: “Encontrá un supermercado cercano que esté abierto en este momento”.

title: “Es una escritora, no una terrorista”: fuerte apoyo de premios Nobel, filósofos y artistas a Sally Rooney
summary: “Es una escritora, no una terrorista”: fuerte apoyo de premios Nobel, filósofos y artistas a Sally Rooney Consideran que la legislación antiterrorista británica y el retiro de la venta de los libros de la autora irlandesa “es un ultraje a los principios básicos de la libertad de expresión y manifest...
content:
“Es una escritora, no una terrorista”: fuerte apoyo de premios Nobel, filósofos y artistas a Sally Rooney
Consideran que la legislación antiterrorista británica y el retiro de la venta de los libros de la autora irlandesa “es un ultraje a los principios básicos de la libertad de expresión y manifestación”
- 3 minutos de lectura'
Hoy, en la prestigiosa revista británica The New Statesman, tres premios Nobel de Literatura, escritores, filósofos y artistas dieron a conocer una breve carta abierta en defensa de la irlandesa Sally Rooney, cuyos libros dejarán de comercializarse en el Reino Unido, según informaron la propia autora y su editorial, Faber. La decisión se debe al apoyo de Rooney al grupo propalestino Palestine Action.
La autora de Gente normal y Conversaciones entre amigoshabía decidido destinar las regalías por las ventas de sus libros en ese territorio a la agrupación de activistas que la Justicia británica evaluó como “terrorista”. Por ende, sus acciones también podrían ser condenadas como tales, estimaron la escritora y la editorial. Rooney considera que el estado de Israel lleva a cabo un genocidio en Gaza.
“Sally Rooney es una escritora, no una terrorista -comienza el comunicado firmado por los premios Nobel de Literatura J.M. Coetzee, Anne Carson y Annie Ernaux-. Sus libros deben estar disponibles para el público. Su retirada de la venta, con base en una legislación antiterrorista mal concebida y draconiana, es un ultraje a los principios básicos de la libertad de expresión y manifestación, tan asumidos como garantizados durante tanto tiempo en este país. Rechazamos categóricamente la censura —ya sea directa o indirecta— e instamos al gobierno a cambiar de rumbo, modificando la legislación que nos ha llevado a este punto de absurdo represivo”.
OPEN LETTER: Sally Rooney is a writer, not a terrorist. Her books must be available to the public. Their withdrawal from sale, on the basis of ill-conceived and draconian anti terror legislation, is an affront to basic principles of free speech and expression so long taken for… pic.twitter.com/QLQel0EC7N
— The New Statesman (@NewStatesman) October 21, 2026
Es la primera vez que la flamante Nobel de Literatura asume una posición pública en un conflicto de “alto perfil”. Los dos protagonistas y el director de la exitosa adaptación televisiva de Gente normal (basada en la novela de Rooney) -Paul Mescal, Daisy Edgar-Jones y Lenny Abrahamson- se unieron al grupo de importantes figuras culturales para firmar una carta abierta en defensa de la autora irlandesa.
Además de los Nobel mencionados, que encabezan el comunicado de apoyo a la escritora, este lleva la firma de reconocidos escritores, artistas y filósofos como Julian Barnes, Slavoj Žižek, Tilda Swinton, Annie Proulx, Zadie Smith, Sally Potter, Naomi Klein, Arundhati Roy, Geroge Saunders, Amitav Ghosh, Kate Nash, Irvine Welsh, Susan Sarandon, Colm Tóibín, Jhumpa Lahiri, Colum McCann y Bella Freud.
En redes sociales, otros escritores y artistas habían apoyado a Rooney.

title: Alquileres de verano: qué localidades de la costa ofrecen mejor margen de ganancia para invertir
summary: Con el verano a pocos meses, resulta interesante analizar cuatro de las localidades más populares de la Costa Atlántica - 6 minutos de lectura' ¿Volvió a ser negocio comprar una propiedad para alquilar? Es la pregunta que vuelve a resonar en un mercado inmobiliario en el que los valores de venta com...
content:
Con el verano a pocos meses, resulta interesante analizar cuatro de las localidades más populares de la Costa Atlántica
- 6 minutos de lectura'
¿Volvió a ser negocio comprar una propiedad para alquilar? Es la pregunta que vuelve a resonar en un mercado inmobiliario en el que los valores de venta comenzaron a recuperarse, aunque en los últimos meses la suba se moderó significativamente, luego de la fuerte caída registrada tras la pandemia.
En la Ciudad de Buenos Aires, la renta bruta anual promedio de un alquiler tradicional se ubicó en 5,7% en agosto de 2026, tomando como referencia un departamento de dos ambientes de 50 m². Esto implica que se necesitan alrededor de 17,6 años de alquiler para recuperar la inversión inicial.
Sin embargo, a la hora de analizar una inversión inmobiliaria, CABA no es la única alternativa. Fuera de los límites porteños aparecen otros destinos que pueden ofrecer rentabilidades similares e, incluso, superiores a las de algunos barrios de la Ciudad. En ese escenario, la pregunta cambia: ¿dónde conviene comprar una propiedad para ponerla en alquiler y obtener una mayor renta?
Y, con el verano a pocos meses, resulta interesante poner bajo la lupa cuatro de las localidades más populares de la Costa Atlántica: Cariló, Pinamar, Villa Gesell y Mar del Plata.
La brecha en la compra
Las diferencias comienzan en el monto necesario para ingresar al mercado. Según un informe de Mirando.ai, startup de inteligencia de mercado para el sector inmobiliario, que analizó más de 33.000 viviendas, los valores presentan una importante dispersión según la localidad y el tipo de propiedad.
Cariló, con aproximadamente 664 viviendas en venta, se posiciona como la localidad más cara entre las analizadas. El metro cuadrado promedio de los departamentos se ubica en US$3333, mientras que el de las casas alcanza los US$1846. “Tres de cada cuatro propiedades publicadas son casas”, especifica el relevamiento.
Le sigue Pinamar, con 5328 viviendas en venta y valores medianos de US$2300/m² para los departamentos y US$1528/m² para las casas.
En Mar del Plata, donde se contabilizan 21.108 propiedades en venta, los departamentos alcanzan un valor medio de US$2062/m², mientras que las casas se ubican en US$1021/m².
Por último, Villa Gesell registra 2319 unidades en venta y presenta los valores más bajos entre las localidades analizadas: US$1310/m² para los departamentos y US$1064/m² para las casas.
Alquilar todo el año: un mercado que casi no existe fuera de Mar del Plata
Pero el precio de compra es solo una parte de la ecuación. Para quien busca adquirir una propiedad como inversión, también resulta fundamental analizar qué posibilidades existen de mantenerla alquilada durante todo el año. Y es acá donde aparecen diferencias importantes entre las localidades.
Fuera de Mar del Plata —donde por cada 1000 viviendas publicadas en venta hay 67 ofrecidas en alquiler anual—, la oferta para contratos de largo plazo es muy reducida. La diferencia es contundente: Pinamar registra casi nueve viviendas en alquiler anual por cada 1000 publicadas en venta; Villa Gesell, apenas cuatro; y Cariló, ninguna.
“Mar del Plata es una ciudad con un mercado de alquiler propio. En las localidades balnearias, en cambio, casi no se ofrecen viviendas para vivir todo el año”, resaltan desde Mirando.ai.
El caso de Cariló es ilustrativo: de los 21 avisos de alquiler que no se presentan explícitamente como temporarios, 17 están publicados en dólares —como es habitual en los alquileres de verano— y ninguno especifica que se trate de una locación anual.
En este escenario, Mar del Plata se diferencia como una alternativa para quien busca comprar una propiedad y mantenerla alquilada durante todo el año: actualmente cuenta con 1407 viviendas ofrecidas bajo esta modalidad.
Pero la cantidad de propiedades disponibles es solo una parte de la ecuación. ¿Qué sucede con la rentabilidad?
Si se toman como referencia los departamentos de un dormitorio, el alquiler anual por metro cuadrado presenta valores relativamente similares en Pinamar y Mar del Plata: $18.750 frente a $17.876, respectivamente. Es decir, alquilar en Pinamar resulta aproximadamente un 5% más caro.
Sin embargo, comprar una propiedad allí cuesta alrededor de un 15% más, una diferencia que termina impactando en el retorno de la inversión: para esta tipología, la rentabilidad bruta anual se ubica en 6,1% en Pinamar frente al 6,6% de Mar del Plata.
En Villa Gesell, el valor del alquiler por metro cuadrado es un 37% inferior al de Mar del Plata, mientras que el precio de compra resulta un 36% más bajo, por lo que la rentabilidad obtenida es similar.
Sin embargo, este último dato debe tomarse únicamente como referencia: el cálculo surge de apenas seis propiedades ofrecidas en alquiler anual, una muestra demasiado pequeña como para considerarla representativa del mercado.
En Cariló no hay suficientes propiedades ofrecidas en alquiler anual como para calcular una rentabilidad representativa.
Rentabilidad: CABA vs. la Costa
Si se toman específicamente departamentos de dos dormitorios —una tipología diferente de la utilizada en la comparación anterior—, la rentabilidad bruta anual alcanza:
- Mar del Plata: 6,1%
- Pinamar: 6,0%
Son porcentajes similares a los registrados en varios barrios porteños:
- Villa Pueyrredón: 6,0%
- Liniers: 6,0%
- San Telmo: 6,0%
- Barracas: 6,0%
- Almagro: 6,1%
- Parque Chacabuco: 6,1%
- Boedo: 6,1%
- Santa Rita: 6,1%
De esta manera, Mar del Plata y Pinamar presentan retornos brutos comparables con algunos de los barrios porteños que rondan el 6% anual.
La brecha se amplía frente a algunos de los barrios más caros de la Ciudad, como Puerto Madero, Palermo y Núñez, donde el elevado precio de compra de las propiedades presiona a la baja la rentabilidad obtenida a través del alquiler.
Alquiler de verano
La ecuación cambia cuando, en lugar de mantener la propiedad alquilada durante todo el año, el propietario apuesta por el alquiler temporario durante la temporad

title: Dónde voto en la Argentina para la segunda vuelta de las elecciones Brasil 2026
summary: Dónde voto en la Argentina para la segunda vuelta de las elecciones Brasil 2026 Tras la primera vuelta electoral, los ciudadanos brasileros que viven en el país se preparan para votar en el balotaje; dónde se deben presentarse - 2 minutos de lectura' Este domingo 25 de octubre, los ciudadanos brasil...
content:
Dónde voto en la Argentina para la segunda vuelta de las elecciones Brasil 2026
Tras la primera vuelta electoral, los ciudadanos brasileros que viven en el país se preparan para votar en el balotaje; dónde se deben presentarse
- 2 minutos de lectura'
Este domingo 25 de octubre, los ciudadanos brasileros que residen en nuestro país votan en el balotaje de Brasil 2026.
Tras los resultados de las elecciones generales quedó establecido que los dos candidatos más votados, el actual presidente Luis Ignacio Lula da Silva y Flávio Bolsonaro, deberán medirse en segunda vuelta para definir quién ocupará el máximo cargo ejecutivo del país.
Las elecciones en el extranjero son organizadas por el Tribunal Electoral de Brasilia y se llevan a cabo en otros países con el apoyo de los Consulados y Embajadas de Brasil.
El Código Electoral estipula un mínimo de 30 votantes como condición para establecer mesas electorales en el extranjero. Preferiblemente, las mesas electorales funcionarán en sedes de embajadas, oficinas consulares o lugares donde se presten servicios del gobierno brasileño.
Dónde voto en la Argentina para la segunda vuelta de las elecciones Brasil 2026
El día de las elecciones, los brasileros que viven en la Argentina y están empadronados deben asistir a las urnas preparadas para emitir su sufragio.
- Fecha y horario: domingo 25 de octubre de 8 a 17.
- Ubicación: Embajada de Brasil en Buenos Aires, Cerrito 1350, CABA
Estos son los documentos válidos para votar:
- Título electoral electrónico con foto (e-Título)
- Documento de identidad (RG)
- Pasaporte brasileño
- Licencia de conducir brasileña (CNH)
- Carnet de categoría profesional reconocido por ley
- Certificado de servicio militar (reservista) con foto;
De acuerdo a lo informado por la Embajada de Brasil, los documentos detallados pueden utilizarse incluso si la fecha de validez ya venció. En tanto, explicaron que los certificados de nacimiento o matrimonio no son válidos como prueba de identidad al momento de votar.

title: ¿Cuándo son las elecciones 2027 en la Argentina? Todas las fechas clave
summary: ¿Cuándo son las elecciones 2027 en la Argentina? Todas las fechas clave Las votaciones generales se ubican en octubre; cuándo es la fecha en caso de que continúen las PASO y cuándo se llevará a cabo un hipotético balotaje - 3 minutos de lectura' El año próximo tiene la particularidad de que concentr...
content:
¿Cuándo son las elecciones 2027 en la Argentina? Todas las fechas clave
Las votaciones generales se ubican en octubre; cuándo es la fecha en caso de que continúen las PASO y cuándo se llevará a cabo un hipotético balotaje
- 3 minutos de lectura'
El año próximo tiene la particularidad de que concentrará nuevamente la atención política por las votaciones a Presidente, que definirán al mandatario por los siguientes cuatro años, y para ello es preciso saber cuándo son las elecciones 2027 en la Argentina y todas las fechas clave del año electoral.
Cuándo son las elecciones 2027 en la Argentina
La elección general presidencial, o primera vuelta, se debe efectuar dentro de los dos meses anteriores a la conclusión del mandato del presidente en ejercicio. Por lo tanto, la votación presidencial de 2027 se debe realizar el domingo 24 de octubre.
En caso de requerirse un balotaje o segunda vuelta electoral, este evento debe darse dentro de los 30 días de celebrada la anterior. Eso significa que el balotaje se haría en noviembre de ser necesario.
Qué pasará con las PASO
El oficialismo busca una reforma electoral que termine con las PASO (Primarias, Abiertas, Simultáneas y Obligatorias). Para ello la Constitución Nacional exige el apoyo de la mayoría absoluta en el Congreso, es decir la mitad más uno de la totalidad de sus miembros. En el caso del Senado, implica el voto afirmativo de 37 senadores.
Al momento, el oficialismo no cuenta con los votos necesarios para suprimir las PASO y, en caso de que se celebren, se llevarán a cabo el domingo 8 de agosto de 2027. Así está establecido por la ley 26.571, que indica que esta votación debe hacerse el segundo domingo de agosto.
Qué se vota en 2027
En las próximas elecciones se elegirán presidente, vicepresidente y se renovarán bancas del Congreso Nacional (130 diputados y 24 senadores).
Sin embargo, la jornada electoral de 2027 no se limitará únicamente a las autoridades nacionales. Los votantes elegirán al jefe de Gobierno de la Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires.
